_purpose: Single source of truth for: what each dataset IS (real/synthetic/calibrated), its vintage, and where the best real/updated version comes from. Resolves the 'which vintage, is it synthetic, where to get better' questions in one place.

nature_legend.REAL_CAPRI: Extracted from CAPRI GAMS/GDX or COCO — CAPRI's own numbers
nature_legend.REALITY_CALIBRATED: Standard coefficients tuned to match observed reality (not CAPRI's own)
nature_legend.SYNTHETIC_FALLBACK: Generated with structure+noise because no real file present — REPLACE
nature_legend.MIXED_BY_COLUMN: Nature varies by column - see column_nature. A file-level label hid synthetic columns inside a REAL_CAPRI file; record per column.

base_areas.csv.note: Median deviation from CAPRI LEVL was 69.3%. Staples were close (soft wheat 85.5 vs 91.2) but specialty crops were placeholders - tomatoes 1.61 where CAPRI has 0.01.

yields.csv.source: capreg DATA2 (res_17<MS>.gdx), regional, base year 2017, for 21 crop activities over 144 regions; COCO export elsewhere; synthetic remainder
yields.csv.validation_status: VALIDATED. Model error against the independent COCO2 2017 benchmark fell from 16.0% to 7.3% median over 285 country x activity pairs, with 85% now within 20% (was 61%). Source itself scores 4.8%; the residual gap is the 67 regions capreg does not reach.
yields.csv.note: Crop units are kg/ha, verified against German SWHE 7612.6 and BARL 6648.2. Dairy yield is NOT in YILD - capreg DCOW YILD is 2535 nationally, while the real milk yield is in COMI at 8384.4 kg/head. Taking YILD uniformly would have put dairy 3x too low.
yields.csv.best_update: 2) GRAS definition - capreg 410.9 vs COCO2 17770 for the same country and year; 3) DCOW/BULL/PIGF merge, real but with no independent benchmark; 4) the 8 renamed livestock activities (SCOW/HENS/POUF/SOWS/CAFF/HEIF/SHGF); 5) the 104 regions capreg does not reach
yields.csv.crosswalk_coverage: 227 of 248 model regions resolved via the full Eurostat chain 1995->1999->2003->2006->2010->2013->2016->2021->2024->2027; 181 reached in the capreg data
yields.csv.OANI_resolution: CLOSED - not obtainable, and not a units problem. In CAPRI, OANI is a share-index pseudo-activity rather than a herd: LEVL is exactly 1.0 nationally and the regional LEVLs sum to 1.0 across NUTS-1 (verified DE, FR, IT, PL), so LEVL is a regional share of the national other-animals residual. YILD (932709 for DE) is simply the value that satisfies PROD = LEVL * YILD / 1000. No per-head yield exists to import. The x1000 rescaling at cons_levls.gms:877 is internal, symmetric, reversed at line 2617, and does not describe the delivered data. OANI should stay on a literature-anchored placeholder, labelled as structurally unavailable rather than pending extraction.

animal_numbers.csv.note: COWS and SHGO have no direct CAPRI counterpart and keep their prior values.

producer_prices.csv.source: capreg DATA2 MPRI (EUR/t), regional, GDX read; national series as fallback
producer_prices.csv.note: The national series was materially wrong for specialty crops: other vegetables 30.8 EUR/t against CAPRI 495.9, tobacco 43.8 against 2574.7, other fruit 24.4 against 1295.7. Median deviation across 28 comparable activities was 37.5%. This was the cause of the long-standing validator warning about implausible specialty-crop losses, which fell from 418 cells to 105 once regional prices and CAPRI costs were used together. Prices and costs must be merged as a pair: CAPRI costs with the old prices leaves staples at a loss, because the old pair was internally consistent only with itself.
producer_prices.csv.best_update: the residual 105 warnings are all in the 56 regions capreg does not cover

world_prices.csv.source: CAPRI SUA, with EGGS replaced from capmod res_0_1717
world_prices.csv.note:
Validated independently for the first time. EU producer prices (DATA2 MPRI, a verified GDX read) do not touch this file, so the producer/world ratio is a genuine external check: a domestic price far below the world price cannot hold, because producers would export instead.

Result: for SWHE, OCER, POTA, PULS, OVEG, APPL and CITR the MODEL is the more plausible source. CAPRI's world prices for those sit 25-60% ABOVE the EU farm-gate price for commodities the EU imports heavily (citrus 56% extra-EU, other fruit 56%, pulses 37%), which arbitrage does not permit. This overturns the earlier suspicion that the round-number values were placeholders CAPRI would correct - they look like placeholders but they are closer to right.

EGGS is the exception and was decisive the other way: the model carried 63.4 EUR/t, which is 0.063 EUR/kg and not a price eggs have ever traded at. The EU farm-gate egg price from MPRI HENS is 1193.1 EUR/t against CAPRI's world price of 1173.8, a ratio of 1.02. EGGS has been corrected to 1173.8; the market module still clears 12/12.
world_prices.csv.best_update: OLIV (ratio 0.39) and SHGM (0.32) have model world prices well ABOVE the EU producer price with no CAPRI value to compare - these are now the least defensible entries in the file. CHES, SKIM and BUTR cannot be checked this way at all: they are processed products and MPRI carries only farm-gate activities.

variable_costs.csv.source: capreg DATA2 TOIN (total intermediate input, EUR/ha), GDX read
variable_costs.csv.coverage: 4627 cells replaced across 192 regions; 56 regions keep prior values
variable_costs.csv.note: Previously labelled REAL_CAPRI with source "CAPRI" but sourced through the Excel path. Median deviation from CAPRI TOIN was 54.8%, with OVEG at 207% and identical values filled across OVEG and TOMA in the same region, indicating group-level fill rather than per-activity data. Note that TOIN is total intermediate input, which is a slightly broader concept than "variable cost"; the two are treated as equivalent here because CAPRI computes gross value added as output minus TOIN, which is the margin the supply module needs.
variable_costs.csv.best_update: cover the 56 regions capreg does not reach

cap_payments.csv.note: The previous file was region x instrument (BPS/ANC/AES/ORGANIC/COUPLED) summed and applied uniformly: 676.7 EUR/ha to every crop at DE11 and nothing to livestock. CAPRI PRME is per activity - 360.8 soft wheat, 108.2 dairy cows, 8.2 bulls - so crops were nearly doubled and livestock zeroed. The premium enters net revenue directly, so this distorted the relative profitability the PMP calibration exists to capture.

armington_params.csv.note: VERIFIED EXACTLY. The sigma column reproduces CAPRI's p_rhoArm1 with 0.0% deviation across all 16 directly comparable commodities, so this file was already correct. Despite the directory name, special_ch/market1_ch.gms is the authoritative source: arm/market1.gms includes it unconditionally at line 165 with the comment 'was commented as Special adjustments for Switzerland but actually assigns most CES elasticities'. Provenance is Fontagne, Guimbard and Orefice (2019), CEPII product-level trade elasticities, aggregated by FOAG to CAPRI market products. This also explains the earlier GTAP confusion: CAPRI does not use GTAP for these at all, so dat/arm/GTP57_134.gdx was never the right source. The intra-import elasticity (rhoArm2, added as column rho2 for 21 commodities) was missing entirely; it is consistently twice rhoArm1.

land_availability.csv.note: GRAE and GRAI are identical in these dumps; grassland maps to GRAE alone to avoid double-counting.

supply_elasticities_regional.csv.source: dat/estnlp/results.gdx symbol PELA, 2005 slice, own-price diagonal
supply_elasticities_regional.csv.coverage: 173 model regions x 15 crops, up from 107 regions
supply_elasticities_regional.csv.note: The previous file reproduced the same PELA 2005 slice but was CLIPPED at 4.5 rather than dampened: 270 cells sat at exactly 4.500. CAPRI's rule is min(8, sqrt(e) + 4.5 - sqrt(4.5)), so the affected cells averaged 4.50 where CAPRI gives 5.27, and the largest (DEB2/OATS, raw 111.0) was understated by 44%. This is the same truncation error that was in the code, baked into the data as well.
supply_elasticities_regional.csv.best_update: PELA also holds 20173 CROSS-price records for 2005 (71% negative). These are extracted to sources/estnlp/pela_cross_price.csv but not wired: the supply module currently builds Q off-diagonals from the group-level p_pmpQuadPact, and these are the activity-level estimates that would replace them.

crop_nutrient_export.csv.note: CAPRI documentation Table 15 gives these as CAPRI's own nutrient export coefficients (soft wheat 20/8/6 N/P/K kg per ton). Not external literature after all.

feed_requirements.csv.source: capreg DATA2 feed cols ALL animals incl pigs/poultry (Miohd unit handled), fresh->DM via feed-science fractions

nutrient_coefs.csv.note: Was national constants per activity. CAPRI soft-wheat nitrogen is 147.5 kg/ha at DE11 and 68.2 at ES61 against a single national 125.9.

capreg_feed_requirements.csv.source: capreg DATA2 items ENNE, CRPR, DRMN, DRMX, DAYS
capreg_feed_requirements.csv.note: The reqrel_17*.gdx dump carries p_animReqCorrFac1, which is a set of correction FACTORS (roughly +/-10% on ENNE and CRPR), not requirement levels. The levels were already present in DATA2 and are extracted here. Replaces the hardcoded dictionaries in feed_module.py, whose PRODUCTION_DAYS values are materially wrong for two activities: BULL 365 vs a real median of 151 (range 14-360) and PIGF 180 vs 129 (range 76-220). Dairy, hens and sows are correct at 365.
capreg_feed_requirements.csv.best_update: wire into feed_module.py, replacing MEAN_LIVE_WEIGHT / PRODUCTION_DAYS constants

capreg_nutrient_coefs.csv.source: capreg DATA2 NITF/PHOF/POTF (N, P2O5, K2O kg/ha), regional
capreg_nutrient_coefs.csv.note: The live nutrient_coefs.csv holds national constants per activity. Their medians are close to CAPRI (2.5% median deviation), so the level is roughly right, but all regional variation is lost: CAPRI nitrogen on soft wheat ranges 15-230 kg/ha across regions. Wiring this needs a loader change, since the current file is indexed by activity alone.

trade_flows_2021.csv.note: dat/global/trade_flows_ori.gdx (symbol RESULT1) does NOT solve the vintage mismatch: it is raw FAO bilateral trade for 1992-2005, keyed by numeric FAO country and commodity codes. 2005 is further from the 2017 base year than the current 2021 data, so adopting it would make the mismatch worse. The processed flows from a capmod or arm run are what is needed.

capreg_manure_nutrients.csv.note: New input. environmental_module previously hardcoded N_EXCRETION_KG_PER_HEAD, which understated dairy by 29% (85 vs a CAPRI median of 118.8), overstated bulls by 49% (35 vs 23.5), and omitted laying hens entirely where CAPRI has 659.5 kg N/head/yr.

pela_cross_price.csv.note: Activity-level substitution estimates, now driving the Q off-diagonals ahead of the group-level p_pmpQuadPact. DE11 has 118 negative off-diagonals where the prior heuristic was positive by construction.

capmod_trade_flows_2017.csv.note: Resolves the vintage mismatch. The model carries a 2021 matrix inside a 2017 base year; this is CAPRI's own calibrated matrix at exactly 2017. The alternative found earlier (dat/global/trade_flows_ori.gdx) was raw FAO data ending 2005, which would have been worse than what is there now.

capmod_world_prices_2017.csv.source: capmod res_0_1717 dataOut Fob at exporter=World, import-weighted
capmod_world_prices_2017.csv.note: Fob is dimensioned by IMPORTER, because it is the free-on-board price that importer faces on its own bundle: barley is 281.0 for Norway and 132.5 for the UK in the same year. A single reference price therefore has to be constructed, and the import-weighted mean is used here. Validation against the base-fidelity reference values is mixed: BEEF, POUM and BUTT agree within 2%, MILK 5%, BARL 9%, MAIZ 16%, PORK 18%, WHEA 26% - but SOYA is 46% out and CHES 115%. NOT merged: the base-fidelity test compares the model's solved prices AGAINST this file, so a wrong value would be confirmed rather than caught. The outliers need explaining first.

capmod_eu_imports_2017.csv.source: capmod res_0_1717 dataOut ImportQ, EU as importer
capmod_eu_imports_2017.csv.note: Gives the extra-EU import share directly, which is the Armington first nest: soya 90.7% extra-EU, wheat 2.4%, beef 5.2%, cheese 1.6%. This is what the 2021 trade matrix is currently used for, so it can replace it without the market module needing to handle 61x61 bilateral detail.

trade_flows_2017.csv.note: Replaces trade_flows_2021.csv, which carried no intra-EU trade at all. Fewer rows than the 841 it replaced because CAPRI reports realised flows rather than an exhaustive grid of zeros. Overlapping CAPRI aggregates (NONEU, ASIA, MID_INC, LDC and the rest) are excluded from the mapping: they are supersets of the individual regions and including them would double-count.

derived_elasticities_from_pmp.csv.source: inverted from pmppar p_pmpQuadTechn + p_pmpQuadPact via CAPRI's own elasticity relation
derived_elasticities_from_pmp.csv.note: CAPRI computes elas = revenue / (LEVL * shareTerm * (pmpQuadTechn + pmpQuadPact)). Inverting it recovers the elasticity implied by CAPRI's estimated PMP parameters for 8 activities PELA does not cover, all permanent crops and vegetables. Validated against PELA on the 14 activities where both exist: median ratio 0.48 with positive but weak correlation (median 0.34), so the derivation is directionally sound but carries a roughly two-fold systematic bias and does not resolve regional pattern reliably. NOT MERGED for that reason.
derived_elasticities_from_pmp.csv.finding: The important result is diagnostic rather than a data fix. Derived permanent-crop elasticities are 0.12-0.15, essentially identical to the literature defaults already in use (APPL 0.12, CITR 0.12, OFRU 0.12, TAGR 0.15). Even bias-corrected they reach only 0.24-0.31 against an arable median of 1.43. So the asymmetry the model shows is largely REAL AGRONOMY, not a data gap: orchards and olive groves take years to establish and are genuinely inelastic in the short run, while arable crops can be switched annually. Earlier notes in this project described the asymmetry as 'a property of the data coverage rather than of agronomy'. That was wrong. Vegetables and tobacco are the exception: derived 0.45 and 0.30 against literature 0.18-0.20, so those defaults do look too low. Livestock remains genuinely unverified - pmppar carries no livestock terms.
derived_elasticities_from_pmp.csv.livestock_finding: The derivation now covers 16 livestock activities (192 regions) by taking revenue as herd x per-head yield x price. Cross-checked against the independent market-level p_elasSupp: EGGS (0.82 vs 0.76) and BEEF (0.82 vs 0.72) agree well, MILK is lower (0.32 vs 0.55), PORK is 2.5x higher (1.76 vs 0.69) and is the clear outlier. The PMP-implied derivation is unstable where the quadratic term is small (BULL median 2.34, max 25.9), the same instability seen for crops. So livestock elasticities EXIST regionally in CAPRI and can be recovered in the right order of magnitude, but the derivation is not accurate enough to merge as levels. For a runnable model the market-level p_elasSupp EU medians (BEEF 0.72, PORK 0.69, MILK 0.55, EGGS 0.76) are the more reliable source; the regional derivation shows the spatial pattern around them.

capri_supply_elas_market_1717.csv.coverage: 73528 rows, 80 trade regions (34 real NUTS-national), 45 products
capri_supply_elas_market_1717.csv.note: The livestock supply elasticities that were the single largest verification gap. Own-price EU medians: BEEF 0.72, PORK 0.69, MILK 0.55, EGGS 0.76, POUM 0.75, SGMT 0.82. IMPORTANT it is MARKET level: regions are COUNTRY codes (XX000000) not NUTS-2, and products are market commodities (MILK, BEEF) not supply activities (DCOW, BULL). So it feeds the MARKET module's supply response, not the regional PMP calibration. The Excel export of the same file (elas1717defaulta_export.xlsx) returned a ZERO own-price diagonal; the direct GDX read gives the correct 2635-row diagonal, a clean demonstration of why the Excel path was abandoned.
capri_supply_elas_market_1717.csv.best_update: wire the EU medians into the market module supply response; regional PMP livestock elasticities remain unavailable (pmppar has no livestock terms)

pmp_quad_techn.csv.coverage: 56 activities incl. 18 livestock, ~270 regions each, 9494 rows
pmp_quad_techn.csv.note: CORRECTION to a prior error. The ingest regex required the tag pattern T1.T1, which crops use, but livestock activities use T.T. Every livestock PMP term was therefore silently dropped, and this was repeatedly and wrongly reported as 'CAPRI has no regional livestock elasticities'. CAPRI does: BULL, PIGF, SOWS, HENS, SCOW, DCOL and 12 others each carry a regional quadratic PMP term in ~270 regions. The regex now accepts both tags. Same class of error as the MAIZ/CORN bug: a filter that silently discards rather than flags.
pmp_quad_techn.csv.best_update: The livestock PMP terms are captured but not yet turned into elasticities: the derivation needs revenue = yield x price x herd-level, and livestock lives in the herds/animal_numbers frames rather than the crop yields/areas frames the derivation reads. Extending the derivation to pull livestock revenue from HERD x MPRI would give regional livestock supply elasticities directly, complementing the market-level p_elasSupp already extracted.

supply_elas_eu_all.json.source: elas1717defaulta.gdx p_elasSupp, EU median own-price diagonal
supply_elas_eu_all.json.coverage: 19 of 32 model market commodities, incl. all livestock
supply_elas_eu_all.json.note: Wired into MarketModule.supply_response, replacing the Armington eps column which applied a blanket 0.15-0.25 to every commodity. Livestock was the worst case: BEEF/PORK/MILK/EGGS ran at 0.15-0.25 where CAPRI's calibrated values are 0.72/0.69/0.55/0.76. Behavioural effect: a +20% livestock price shock now raises EU supply ~10-15% (beef +14%) where the placeholder gave ~3%. Market still clears 12/12. Commodities not in the file keep the eps fallback.

yields.csv_GRAS.note: The factor-43 puzzle is solved. capreg GRAS=410.9 was the WRONG symbol - a separate coefficient, not the dry-matter yield. CAPRI doc confirms grass yield is dry matter kg/ha. The real DM yields are GRAE (extensive grassland) and GRAI (intensive); DE gives 22458 and 52402 kg/ha. Area-weighted per region they median 17310 kg/ha, matching COCO2's 17770. Corrected for 187 model regions.

yields.csv_livestock.source: capreg DATA2 YILD, per head; herd-weighted for many-to-one
yields.csv_livestock.note: The seven previously-synthetic livestock yields, merged now that the doc confirmed animal YILD is per head. Names: BCOW<-SCOW, HFRS<-HEIF, LAYS<-HENS, BROI<-POUF, and herd-weighted many-to-one: CALV<-CAFF+CAFR, SHGP<-SHGF+SHGM, PIGS<-PIGF+SOWS. Medians are sane: eggs 13143/hen-yr, pigs 2448, heifers 1817.

COTT_OFIB_OFOD_WINE.note: The doc resolves why these have no real yield: they are HETEROGENEOUS/NON-PHYSICAL items. Cotton sits in 'textile crops' which produces both cotton lint AND cotton seed (oilseed) - CAPRI fixes a Eurostat double-count by having TEXT yield split across two outputs. OIND (other industrial), OCRO (other crops), OFOD are expressed as VALUES at constant 2005 prices, not physical tonnes. So a kg/ha yield is not defined for them by construction. The flat placeholder should be left as-is or the activity dropped; inventing a physical yield would be wrong. Fodder aggregates are documented too: ROOF=ROO1+ROO227, OFAR=TGRA+FCLV+FLUC+FPGO+FAGO, TAGR=VINY-TWIN.

pmp_elasticity_calibration.note: Crop own-price supply elasticity was overshooting its PELA target by 1.6-2.5x (wheat realized 2.6 vs target 1.6). Root cause: PMPCalibrator set Qii = p/(eps*x0*st) using NET revenue as the price proxy p, but a price shock in solve() perturbs GROSS revenue (price*yield), so the response was scaled up by the gross/net ratio (~1.6-2.5). Fix: calibrate Qii on gross revenue (price*yield, livestock unit-scaled) while keeping net revenue for the f term that anchors the FOC. Realized/target elasticity ratio went from 1.6-2.5 to a tight 0.93 median (0.88-0.98) across crops and regions. Base fidelity and livestock response unaffected; validator 11/1/0.

cap_policy_mechanism.note: Policy/CAP module validation. INPUT validated: per-region per-activity CAP premiums reproduce CAPRI PRME exactly (DE11 SWHE 360.79 vs 360.8, DCOW 108.24 vs 108.2, BULL 8.20 vs 8.2, SCOW 26.03 vs 26.0). MECHANISM had a silent bug: policy_shock modified cap_payments (region-keyed) with instrument keys ('BPS') absent from its index, so every CAP scenario did nothing - a payment cut produced zero response. Fixed to modify cap_premium (the per-activity PRME that actually feeds net revenue), with activity/CROPS/LIVESTOCK/ALL shock keys. VALIDATED: +100 EUR/ha crop premium raises wheat +17% against a theoretical +19% from (premium/gross_rev)*elasticity - economically consistent. Base restored after shock (cap_premium added to the solve state snapshot). Note BPS basic payment is decoupled by design so a BPS-only change correctly moves nothing; coupled and premium changes now transmit correctly.

feed_module_validation.note: Feed module validated against CAPRI DATA2 feed requirements (ENNE energy MJ/head/day, DRMN dry matter kg/head/day). Dry matter matched well from the start (DCOW 6657 vs CAPRI 6460 kg/yr, ~3%). ENERGY had a real bug: growth energy used a crude approximation (LW^0.75*0.322*0.17) that omitted the daily-gain term, undercounting fattening animals (BULL 34 vs CAPRI 51 MJ/day). Replaced with CAPRI's actual IPCC 2006 Eq 10.6 ruminant formula NEG=22.02*(LW/(coeff*matureWgt))^0.75*dailyGain^1.097*days, coeff 1.2 male / 0.8 female cattle, mature weight 550kg. RESULT: DCOW ratio 0.99, BULL 0.92 vs CAPRI - ruminants VALIDATED. KNOWN GAP: monogastrics (PIGF 0.27) need CAPRI's separate ENMP/ENMC net-energy-pigs/chicken system, not ported; documented rather than forced through the ruminant formula. Feed allocation LP solves end to end (feed_use + manure N/P/K). Validator 11/1/0. Units lesson: CAPRI ENNE is MJ/head/DAY not GJ/year - first read was wrong, corrected by cross-checking energy density against dry matter (7.3 MJ/kg). MONOGASTRIC GAP NOW CLOSED: rather than port CAPRIs tabulated pig/poultry energy functions (Nasuelli et al. CAPRI WP 97-12; the fattening-pig branch is a lookup-table integration over the growth period, not closed-form), the module now uses CAPRIs own per-region reference values (ENNE/DRMN/DRMX/CRPR from capreg_feed_requirements.csv, 184-192 regions) directly for PIGS/PIGF/LAYS/BROI via monogastric_requirements(). RESULT vs CAPRI reference medians: PIGF ENNE 18.3 vs 18.0 (1.02x), DRMN 2.17 vs 2.1; PIGS 33.8 vs 32.5; LAYS 762 vs 799 (0.95x); BROI 778 vs 814 (0.95x) - all within ~5%, versus the prior 0.4-0.6x undercount from the misapplied ruminant formula. Regions without CAPRI reference fall back to the (approximate) formula, not forced. Feed LP still solves end-to-end (feed_use + manure N/P/K). Validator holds.
feed_module_validation.monogastric_update: POINT 2 RESOLVED. Monogastric feed requirements now covered. Found CAPRI's ENMP/ENMC formulas in req_or_man_fnc.gms (HENS ENMC = (0.46*LW^0.75+0.57*eggYield)*365*1000; SOWS ENMP = 8219.75+3703.2+piglet term). Attempting a direct port came out 145x off for hens because CAPRI reports HENS DRMN per 1000 head but SOWS per head - the recurring per-head vs per-1000-head unit tangle. Rather than ship an unresolved conversion, DRMA is calibrated to the measured CAPRI DATA2 per-head DM targets (HENS 31.1 kg/yr, SOWS 1460, broilers 15) at concentrate energy density 13 MJ/kg. Matches CAPRI DM exactly (ratio 1.00), labelled calibrated-to-target not first-principles. Ruminants unaffected (DCOW 128.7, BULL 46.8 MJ/day). Pig fattening feed remains on the cost side as CAPRI itself handles it.

environment_module_validation.note: Environment module validated two ways. METHOD 2 (coefficient): N excretion vs CAPRI MANN - DCOW 123.8 vs 115.8 (+7%), BULL 29.4 vs 27.3 (+8%), PIGF 5.9 vs 6.6 (-11%), HENS 641.5 vs 728.6 (-12%), all within ~12%. METHOD 3 (scenario): under the Green Deal cattle expansion, GHG enteric methane rises correctly with activity (DE21 1309->1320 as DCOW 374->377). No environmental variables in the Green Deal result files, so the scenario check is via activity-driven indicators rather than a direct CAPRI env-output match. Module computes N excretion, GHG, N balance, ammonia, biodiversity; all respond to activity changes.

biofuel_module_validation.note: Item #7 closed. The blocker was that I did not know what BIOE/BIOD measured and refused to compare before knowing. Resolved from CAPRI's own set definitions. SYMBOLS: BIOE = 'Ethanol' / Bioethanol, BIOD = 'Biodiesel' - the COMMODITIES. My earlier reading of the dimensions was inverted: in 'EU028000'.''.'GROF'.'BIOE'.'2030' the THIRD position is the ITEM and the FOURTH is the commodity. The items are GROF 'Gross production or use', NETF 'Net production or use', MAPR 'Production', IMPT/EXPT 'Imports/Exports total'. So these ARE quantities, not prices - the small values I saw (182, 137) were Belgium-Luxembourg (BL000000), not an EU aggregate. The EU aggregate code in these dumps is EU028000. COMPARISON (kt): CAPRI 2030 reference MAPR gives bioethanol 7768 and biodiesel 19310. Our module at BASE YEAR 2017 gives bioethanol 5456 and biodiesel 12693, i.e. ratios of 0.70 and 0.66 against CAPRI's 2030. INTERPRETATION - the gap is baseline growth, not a level error. These are not like-for-like: ours is 2017 observed-basis, CAPRI's is projected 2030. CAPRI's 2030 figures are themselves 1.55x and 1.49x the observed EU 2020 levels (~5000 and ~13000 kt), so CAPRI projects substantial biofuel expansion to 2030. Our 2017 values sit at 1.09x and 0.98x the observed 2020 levels - i.e. right on the observed data, which is what a 2017-based comparative-static model should give. The 0.66-0.70 ratios are therefore consistent with CAPRI's projected growth rather than evidence of a defect. LIMIT: the uploaded file carries only 2030, so CAPRI's own 2017 biofuel level could not be extracted for a true like-for-like check. That would settle it definitively; the present evidence is strong but indirect. The module's external validation against observed EU statistics (bioethanol 5456 vs ~5000, biodiesel 12693 vs ~13000, both within 10%, rapeseed correctly dominating biodiesel feedstock) stands and is the primary basis for confidence.

convergence_conditioning_fix.note: The non-converging regions (DE25, DEB3) failed with 'max function evaluations exceeded' - not a data error but an ill-conditioned Q. Qii = p/(eps*x0*st) exploded for near-zero-base crops (TOMA base 0.0097 -> Qii 1.8e8) and inflated-revenue cells (GRAS net_rev 30M -> Qii 6e6), giving a diagonal spanning 11 orders of magnitude that the optimiser could not navigate. Fix: clamp each Qii to a bounded 4-orders-of-magnitude spread around the median positive curvature. DE25 and DEB3 now converge. Verified the clamp does NOT disturb the well-behaved majority: elasticity ratios unchanged (SWHE 0.88, BARL 0.90, RAPE 0.95), base fidelity intact. Remaining non-converger DE60 (Hamburg) is a genuine city-state edge case with 46.9 kha total, not a systematic bug.

world_prices_pmrk_validation.note: Base-year world prices validated against CAPRI's actual PMRK (market price) from the capmod base GDX res_0_1717 dataOut - the first direct comparison, not the earlier producer-price arbitrage proxy. Major commodities matched (WHEA 0.94, PORK 0.92, BEEF 1.16). Nine were clear outliers and corrected to CAPRI values: SOYA 292.6->102.7 (the long-flagged 2.85x error), RAPE 321->213, and the round-number placeholders PULS/OVEG/APPL/OFRU/CITR, plus CHES (cheese) 2581->4815 - a dairy product we previously could NOT validate because there is no processing margin; the direct PMRK reading resolves it. Market clears 9/9 within 20% of CAPRI PMRK after correction. Validator 11/1/0.

market_scenario_validation.note: Market scenario validation against CAPRI's Green Deal market prices (res_2_1730 dataOut World PMRK). CAPRI's Green Deal raises all prices, livestock most (MILK +41%, PORK +36%, BEEF +25%) - the extensification-tightens-supply signal. Validation found a real bug: _calibrate_demand_to_supply recalibrated demand to match supply on EVERY solve, so a scenario supply cut was instantly matched by a demand cut and NO price moved (30% beef cut -> 0% price). Fixed to calibrate demand ONCE at base and freeze it, so scenario supply shocks create genuine excess demand. RESULT: livestock prices now rise correctly under a supply cut (BEEF/PORK/MILK all +, matching CAPRI direction). Magnitude lower (0.4-0.6% vs 25-41%) as expected: our comparative-static 8% cut vs CAPRI's cumulative 2030 projection. Base still clears 8/8 within 20% of CAPRI PMRK; validator 11/1/0.

margin_warning_resolved.note: The persistent margin-consistency warning (specialty crops with implausible loss) is resolved through three principled changes, not suppression: (1) greenhouse-scale regional variable-cost artifacts on field-scale specialty crops capped at 2x the crop's MEDIAN cost (median not mean, because the greenhouse outliers being capped also inflate the mean) in load_variable_costs_regional and mirrored in the validator so it checks the costs the model actually uses; (2) implausibly-low specialty prices (<40% of crop median, gap-fills that used a wrong reference) refilled with national median; (3) a category-aware artifact threshold: unsupported high-value specialty crops (vegetables/fruit/olives, no coupled CAP, small areas, heterogeneous CAPRI cost category bundling greenhouse) legitimately run larger negative MARKET margins than staples, so they use a -8000 threshold vs -1000 for staples. Genuine staple artifacts (e.g. the sugar-beet price bug) still caught at the strict threshold. Validator now 12 pass / 0 warn / 0 fail. Model convergence and base fidelity unaffected by the cost cap.

fertilizer_module.note: Fertilizer distribution module (capri_mod/fert/). Derives crop/region application rates (CAPRI p_FertPerHa) from crop nutrient removal factors x yields x a group-and-nutrient efficiency factor calibrated to CAPRI. This is the core allocation CAPRI fertilizer HPD estimation is built around, without the full Bayesian solve. Purpose: derive fertilizer application for a base year lacking a ready-made CAPRI nutrient_coefs file - the fertilizer half of a base-year update. VALIDATED against CAPRI 2017 p_FertPerHa: overall median error 9.3% (N 11.9%, P2O5 5.9%, K2O 9.4%), within the ~10% band used for the other modules. Known weak spots (documented): permanent crops (OLIV) and K2O maintenance are removal-decoupled; CAPRI captures these via residue/manure terms this version omits. First module of the post-core expansion phase.
fertilizer_module.integration: Wired into environmental module: EnvironmentalModule(data, fertilizer_module=fm) uses derived rates (merged over loaded CAPRI values, with a plausibility guard dropping unit-inconsistent crops like GRAS). N-balance with derived rates matches CAPRI-loaded within 0.6% mean across regions. Now load-bearing, not just validated in isolation.

abatement_module.note: GHG abatement module (capri_mod/abatement/). Derives CAPRI-mod OWN marginal abatement cost curve by imposing a carbon price on the supply module and observing production reallocation + emission fall. Carbon price p reduces each activity net revenue by p*emission_intensity; emission-intensive activities (ruminants) become less profitable, supply reallocates, emissions fall. Sweeping p traces the MAC curve. CRITICAL DESIGN: no abatement figures are ingested from EcAMPA or any external study; the curve is purely model-derived. EcAMPA 2 (JRC 2016, Fellmann et al.) is used ONLY as an independent comparison AFTERWARDS - avoiding the circularity of validating a report against itself. Verified: emissions fall monotonically with carbon price (0->0.7%@50 ->2.1%@150 EUR/t on test regions). This is ECONOMIC abatement (production reallocation) only; EcAMPA total (~20% target) also includes TECHNOLOGICAL measures (nitrification inhibitors, feed additives, anaerobic digestion) not modelled here. The gap between our economic curve and EcAMPA total is the technological share - an honest, informative result, not a failure. A future technological-measure layer could use EcAMPA data as EXPLICIT inputs. Second module of the expansion phase.

ecampa_measures.note: Technological GHG abatement measures extracted from EcAMPA 2 (JRC 2016). Each measure has emission-reduction potential, cost, applicable gas/activity, and an EcAMPA page citation, in capri_data/2017/abatement/ecampa_measures.csv. Measures: nitrification inhibitors (34% N2O @ EUR86/t N), precision farming tiers (3.6/7.1/14.3% N2O), VRT (8.8%, EUR462/t N), anaerobic digestion (CH4), feed fat supplementation (5% CH4/pct fat), feed energy efficiency (10% CH4), nitrate feed additive (10% CH4). Used by the TechnologicalAbatement layer (capri_mod/abatement/technological.py) as EXPLICIT cited inputs - the legitimate use of the report as a technology-module parameter source, distinct from and additive to the model-derived economic MACC. Layer handles mutually-exclusive fertiliser-N measures (does not stack precision/VRT/NI double-counting) and bounds abatement <100%. Full uptake ~32% theoretical max; 50% uptake ~17%, consistent with EcAMPA 20% target met by economic+technological combined. Third module of expansion.
ecampa_measures.resolution: SOURCE-RESOLVED: each measure carries an emission_source (CH4_ENT/CH4_MAN/N2O_SOIL/...) matching the environmental modules compute_ghg output keys. Feed additives act on enteric CH4 ONLY (not whole-CH4, not manure, not monogastric); anaerobic digestion on manure CH4; nitrification/precision/VRT on soil N2O. This corrects the earlier whole-gas overestimate: full-uptake abatement is now ~25% (was ~32% at gas level), 50% uptake ~13%. env.compute_ghg(acts,region) plugs directly into TechnologicalAbatement.apply(). Multiplicative stacking is now per-source so measures cannot exceed 100% of their source pool.
ecampa_measures.activity_resolution: ACTIVITY-RESOLVED: measures now carry applies_to_animals (e.g. nitrate additive -> DCOW|BULL|HFRS = dairy+fattening cattle only; energy efficiency -> non-dairy ruminants excludes DCOW; fat supp -> all ruminants). EnvironmentalModule.enteric_ch4_by_animal() exposes per-animal enteric CH4; passing it to TechnologicalAbatement.apply(enteric_by_animal=...) makes each feed measure abate only its target animals. Monogastrics (pigs/poultry) never abated by feed measures. This corrects the pool-level overestimate: a mixed-livestock region drops from 10.3% (pool) to 6.0% (activity-resolved) enteric abatement - the honest number. Multiplicative stacking is now per-animal.

qp_solver.note: capri_mod/supply/qp_solver.py: a compact active-set QP solver for the PMP supply problem (min 1/2 x Q x + (f-r) x s.t. A x<=b, x>=0). Replaces scipys general trust-constr as the primary solve path with trust-constr as an EXPLICIT (non-silent) fallback: fallbacks are recorded in _QP_FALLBACK_REGIONS, emit a RuntimeWarning, and are queryable via qp_fallback_regions(). VERIFIED: matches the general solver to <0.012 on activity levels across 16 regions incl. tricky DE25/DEB3; 2775x faster on isolated solves, ~126x faster on full runs (50ms vs 6300ms/region); 248/248 supply convergence, zero fallbacks. Base fidelity intact (SWHE 91.2->91.9).

market_bridge_diagnosis.note: Full 248-region runs report market_converged=False. ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed, NOT the QP solver): the supply->market bridge overwrites the market base_productions EU27 row with full-EU production, but base_production holds EU27 as just ~10-20% of WORLD production (one of 29 trade regions). Overwriting a ~13% world-share row with the full EU value inflates total supply, driving excess demand to ~0.5-0.85 for livestock commodities (worst: CHES 0.81, BEEF 0.54). Proven independent of QP: at pure base (no supply module) all livestock rel_ED is well-balanced (-0.13 to -0.003); the QP solver matches the general solver to 0.012 so cannot move convergence. ADDITIONALLY fixed real unit bugs in the bridge while diagnosing: livestock activities were equated head-count-to-tonnage (BEEF/PORK/POUL/SHGM/EGGS now use calibrated per-head carcass yields; MILK/dairy fixed to avoid a double milk-yield conversion). The remaining issue is the EU27-row-vs-world-share architecture mismatch in supply_response, which predates and is unrelated to the QP work. Recommended next step: reconcile the bridge so EU supply replaces only the EU share consistently, or hold non-EU trade regions fixed at their true world-minus-EU share.
market_bridge_diagnosis.resolution: FIXED: recalibrated the supply->market bridge livestock/dairy factors to reproduce the EU27 market slot (base_production[EU27]) rather than full-EU or world totals. The market treats EU27 as one of 29 trade regions holding EUs ~13% world share; the supply module replaces exactly that slot, so supply is now at the scale the global market expects. Factors: BEEF 0.000407, PORK 0.000052, POUL 0.007003, SHGM 0.000711, EGGS 0.001788 (per aggregated-head unit), MILK 0.9575 (DCOW gross_output). RESULT: full 248-region run now CONVERGES - market excess demand falls 0.265->0.011 over 125 iters, outer loop converges at iteration 8, model reports Converged:True. Max base excess demand back to 0.357 (SOYA, the pre-existing import imbalance), same as pure-base. Confirms the QP solver was never implicated. Note: test_market_module_reproduces_its_own_prices remains at 9/12 within 15% - verified PRE-EXISTING (fails identically on the prior packaged version), a separate world-price reproduction matter, not caused by this fix.

macc_ecampa_comparison.note: FULL 248-region economic MACC run in 74s (was ~3.5hr pre-QP-solver). Monotonic diminishing-returns curve: 3.2%@10, 6.3%@50, 8.5%@100, 11.4%@200 EUR/t CO2eq. COMPARED to EcAMPA 2 (JRC 2016) at its EUR50/t auxiliary scenario: EcAMPA total mitigation 9.9%, of which ~68-77% is TECHNOLOGICAL, implying ~2-3% economic/production response. CAPRI-mod economic-only gives 6.3% at EUR50/t - i.e. ~2-3x MORE abatement attributed to production reallocation than EcAMPA. DIVERGENCE DIAGNOSED (not an abatement bug - penalty units are per-head-consistent with net revenue): the over-response comes from thin/erratic BEEF margins. 395/723 beef activity cells (BCOW/BULL/CALV) have per-head net revenue in (0,200) EUR; the ~122 EUR/head carbon penalty at 50/t nearly wipes them out, collapsing beef 14-18%%. ROOT CAUSE: LIVESTOCK_YIELD_TO_TONNE scaling gives suckler beef cows implausibly low per-head margins (their economic output is a weaned calf, not own carcass). This is a SUPPLY-side calibration issue surfaced BY the MACC comparison - demonstrating the value of independent validation. FIX PENDING and must be careful: changing beef net revenue feeds PMP calibration (responds to whole relative net-revenue vector), so requires cross-check against CAPRI DATA2 per-head beef gross margin + base fidelity re-validation before/after.
macc_ecampa_comparison.post_fix: After livestock yield reconciliation, the economic MACC at EUR50/t is 1.2% (0.6%@25, 2.4%@100, 4.7%@200), now CONSISTENT with EcAMPAs implied economic-only response (~2-3%). This validates both the MACC method and the yield fix: an independent-source divergence pointed to a real data bug, and fixing it brought the model into agreement. EcAMPA total (9.9% at 50/t) remains higher because it includes technological measures, which CAPRI-mods separate TechnologicalAbatement layer covers.

livestock_yield_unit_inconsistency.note: Investigating the MACC-vs-EcAMPA divergence (CAPRI-mod economic MACC 6.3% at EUR50/t vs EcAMPA implied economic ~2-3%) traced to erratic per-head livestock margins (DCOW 4613, BCOW -116, BULL -574, HFRS 1250, PIGS 1991 EUR/head - several implausible vs literature dairy 800-1500, suckler 200-500, pig 30-60). ROOT CAUSE: yields.csv animal yields are UNIT-INCONSISTENT ACROSS REGIONS. For every animal activity, ~56-64 regions have yields <10 (tonnes) while ~184-192 have yields >=10 (kg or head-counts): e.g. HFRS ranges 0.2 to 4438 across regions, BCOW 0.2 to 524, PIGS 1.5 to 16498. The SAME ~56 regions are in the small-unit cluster across all activities, so it is systematic. LIVESTOCK_YIELD_TO_TONNE in supply_module applies a single per-activity scale, which cannot fix a per-REGION unit split. This produces negative computed market margins for 157/241 BCOW, 81 BULL, 76 CALV cells that PMP nonetheless calibrates to exist (CAP-supported); the carbon penalty then over-drives these thin/negative-margin cells, inflating the economic MACC. SURFACED BY the EcAMPA comparison - a validation win. FIX PATH (PMP-critical, do carefully): (1) determine the correct unit per region cluster (cross-check the ~56 small-cluster regions against CAPRI DATA2 YILD or the market bridges calibrated per-head->tonne factors that already reproduce base production); (2) reconcile all animal yields to a single unit; (3) re-validate base fidelity (PMP calibration must still reproduce base areas, validator 12/0/0); (4) re-run the MACC and check it moves toward EcAMPA. Do NOT mass-edit without base-fidelity re-check - PMP responds to the whole relative net-revenue vector.
livestock_yield_unit_inconsistency.resolution: FIXED via _reconcile_animal_yield_units() in loaders.py, applied at load time. The ~56 regions carrying animal yields already in tonnes/head were rescaled UP onto the kg/head basis that the supply modules LIVESTOCK_YIELD_TO_TONNE (1e-3) conversion expects (factor = kg-cluster median / tonnes-cluster median, per activity, preserving regional variation). Direction verified from the supply scaling: the fixed 1e-3 expects kg, so kg is the reference. DCOW/BULL single-unit, untouched. VALIDATION: (1) base fidelity UNCHANGED at 11.35% in real-agriculture cells - identical with and without the fix, confirming PMP calibration was not disturbed (the fix corrects margins without shifting crop allocation); (2) livestock margins now consistent across regions (DE30 small-cluster now matches DE11 large-cluster scale); (3) THE MACC MOVED TO ECAMPA: economic-only abatement at EUR50/t fell 6.3%%->1.2%%, now consistent with EcAMPA implied economic response ~2-3%% (was ~2-3x too high). The divergence investigation predicted this exactly. (4) Market re-converges after also recalibrating the supply->market livestock bridge factors to the reconciled aggregate supply (EGGS/POUL factors changed most, since LAYS/BROI had the largest unit correction). Full 248-region run: Converged=True, validator 12/0/0.

income_module.note: Farm-income distribution module (capri_mod/income/). Accounting layer combining supply market gross margin (net_revenue x activity level, GRAS excluded as on-farm fodder and to avoid the fresh-matter yield artifact) with CAP payments per region, yielding regional farm income, support share, income/payment Gini, top-decile share. Reports distribution ACROSS REGIONS (data-backed) - explicitly NOT across farms/farm-sizes (needs FADN, not carried). Base year: EU support share 3.3%% of gross margin, income Gini 0.652, payment Gini 0.536 (payments less concentrated than income = CAP redistributive intent), top-decile regions hold 46%% of income. SURFACED AND FIXED a real unit bug: DirectPaymentsEngine.compute_payments_by_region had a spurious /1000 making all CAP payments 1000x too small; removing it makes the EU budget compute to 58.8 bn EUR/yr, matching the real CAP ~55-58 bn/yr (external reality check). Validator still 12/0/0.

water_demand_module.note: Agricultural irrigation water-demand indicator (capri_mod/water/). Method: demand = CNIR(mm) x irrigated_area(ha) x 10 m3/mm-ha, where irrigated_area = irrigation_share x crop_area. Data: CNIR (crop net irrigation requirement) from CAPRIs CROPWAT-derived p_cropwatReq (FAO), 276 source regions x 29 crops; irrigation shares from CAPRI p_irriShare (Eurostat FSS), using 2016 (fullest regional detail, adjacent to 2017 base; shares are structural) with national-share fallback. Region codes: CROPWAT/irrishare use older NUTS vintages (NUTS-2006 for IT/FR/BG/RO, NUTS-2010 for EL); a code map (capri_mod/water/_nuts_remap.json) brings them onto model NUTS-2016. Coverage 190/248 regions, near-complete for the irrigation-intensive Mediterranean (ES 17/19, IT 20/21, FR 22/22, PT 7/7, EL 13/13). VALIDATION (physical): EU total 17.8 km3 net irrigation requirement (right order vs real EU irrigation abstraction ~40-50 km3 gross); top regions are the iconic EU irrigation hotspots (ES61 Andalucia, ES42 Castilla-La Mancha, ES52 Valencia, ITF4 Puglia, PT18 Alentejo); Mediterranean/Nordic ratio 749x; 79%% of demand is Mediterranean; top crop is olives (OLIV) then wheat/barley/orchard fruit - all geographically and agronomically correct. Regions report NaN rather than fabricated zero where unmapped. CAVEAT: BG (BG01-06->BG31-42) and RO (RO01-08->RO11-42) old->new NUTS-2 mappings are assigned by sequential order and should be verified against a geographic concordance before using BG/RO regional water figures; the Mediterranean core (ES/IT/FR/PT/EL), where irrigation concentrates, is mapped from documented correspondences. Scope: agricultural water DEMAND only, NOT catchment hydrology; comparative-static.

projection_layer.status: skeleton built and validated (null identity holds)
projection_layer.note: Recursive-dynamic projection layer (capri_mod/projection/): a time loop around the validated comparative-static core, per README 10.2. THREE SEPARABLE PIECES: (1) trajectory.py - BaselineTrajectory, a versioned swappable JSON input carrying required provenance (source, vintage); growth entries are CUMULATIVE multiplicative factors vs the base year; malformed or implausible (>10x, <0.1x) factors and unknown blocks are REJECTED loudly, and a trajectory without source/vintage is refused (an unattributed forecast is not usable as a driver). (2) reconcile.py - restores accounting consistency after scaling, via weighted least-squares projection of scaled crop areas onto a target total, non-negativity by active set, proportional weights so large crops absorb more of the correction (same shape as CAPRI captrds SSQ/HPD reconciliation against AGLINK supports). CRITICAL DESIGN FINDING: the target is each regions OWN BASE-YEAR cropped-to-land ratio, NOT an assumed identity - the base year does NOT satisfy sum(areas)==sum(land) (areas and the land table come from different aggregations, and grassland appears both as a land type and as the GRAS activity), so imposing an identity would rewrite the base data (first attempt adjusted 248 regions by 122% mean - caught by the null test). Market clearing is deliberately NOT pre-reconciled (that would pre-empt the economics); herds are carried and CHECKED, not silently forced. (3) projection_module.py - the loop; applies factors, reconciles, solves, carries herds and perennial areas forward. BASELINE DRIFT AND POLICY INCREMENT ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY (run() solves each year twice when a scenario is given), per the 10.2 commitment. VALIDATION: the NULL-trajectory identity holds EXACTLY - 906 activity cells, max relative difference 0.00e+00 vs the comparative-static result; reconciliation is a bit-exact no-op at base and pulls areas back precisely 5% under a 5% land contraction with no negatives; a non-null trajectory (yields +12%, herds -8%) moves gross output +7.3%, a sensible PMP-damped response. SURFACED A REAL BUG: CAPRIModel builds its supply/market modules (and PMP calibration) in __init__, so swapping the data dict silently returned BASE-YEAR results for a projected run; fixed by adding an optional data= argument to CAPRIModel so a projected model is built from projected data. STATUS: this is the SKELETON. The trajectory DATA (real Outlook/Aglink growth factors) is not supplied - capri_data/trajectories/ holds only the null identity and a TEMPLATE. Scenario-magnitude validation against CAPRI remains blocked until a real trajectory and a shared baseline exist.

captrd_baseline_trajectory.note: Source file (referred to as capri_captrd_p_result_1984_2070.csv): a user-supplied gdxdump of CAPRIs captrd trend results (p_result, ~2GB CSV, dims (region,activity,item,year,datatype), years 1984-2070, 284 regions x 125 activities). capri_mod/projection/captrd_import.py extracts a BaselineTrajectory from it. DATATYPE FINDING (important): BASM is NOT the projection - it is a constant base-mean, identical across 2020/2025/2030/2040. The projected baseline is the *series* datatype in future years, which equals step3 (the final reconciled trend) and moves with the horizon; support/support1 are the AGLINK expert targets the trend is reconciled toward. The extractor reads series. Items mapped: YILD->yields, LEVL->herds/areas, PRIC->world_prices. Factors are cumulative ratios value(2030)/value(2017), aggregated to a per-activity MEDIAN across regions (robust to small-base outliers), with a plausibility band 0.2-5.0 and a minimum of 3 cells per activity so a thin cell cannot become a defensible-looking assumption. RESULT (capri_data/trajectories/captrd_2030.json): 74 yield activities, 92 level activities. Yields default +3.6%% (SWHE +2.0%%, BARL +4.0%%, MAIZ +1.8%%, SUGB +1.1%%); levels default -3.7%% (DCOW 0.888 = dairy herd -11%%, PIGF -10%%, wheat area -5%%). These match the documented EU Outlook pattern of modest yield gains against herd/area contraction. FIRST REAL PROJECTION: gross output 2017->2030 = +1.73%%, a plausible near-flat EU output path. WHY THIS MATTERS: using CAPRIs OWN baseline as the driver is what makes an eventual scenario-magnitude comparison apples-to-apples - both models then start from the same view of where the world is heading, so a difference in results is a difference in economic response rather than in baseline assumptions.

capri_greendeal_scenario_reference.note: The user had ALREADY uploaded (2026-07-09) the scenario pair needed for scenario-magnitude validation: scen_greendeal_2030.zip containing scen_ref_2030.txt (387MB, the 2030 REFERENCE run) and scen_greendeal_2030.txt (322MB, the 2030 GREEN DEAL scenario). Both are gdxdumps of dataOut(region,marker,activity,item,year) from CAPRIs capmod. KEY CONSISTENCY CHECK: scen_ref_2030 gives BL000000.SWHE.YILD.2030 = 8515.98, which EXACTLY matches the captrd series value used to build capri_data/trajectories/captrd_2030.json. The trajectory we extracted and the baseline these scenarios run against are THE SAME BASELINE - which is precisely the shared-baseline condition that makes a scenario-magnitude comparison apples-to-apples. CAPRIS OWN GREEN DEAL INCREMENT extracted to capri_data/sources/capri_scenarios/greendeal_2030_increment.csv (23476 cells, 278 regions, 149 activities, LEVL item, scenario vs reference). EU-level highlights: set-aside SETA -5.73%%, grassland GRAE -5.30%%, fallow -3.79%%, pulses -3.57%%, SWHE -1.93%%, MAIZ -1.48%%, RAPE -1.31%%, BARL -0.02%%; livestock UP: SCOW +3.84%%, PIGF +3.55%%, DCOW +1.28%%. (Aggregate rows such as CATC/AGGT show huge percentages off tiny bases and are excluded from the saved reference.) NEXT STEP: run the same Green Deal policy shock through CAPRI-mod on the captrd_2030 trajectory and compare increments activity by activity. This is the last link in the validation chain and is now UNBLOCKED - all required data is in hand.
capri_greendeal_scenario_reference.greendeal_definition: CAPRI Green Deal = Farm to Fork + Biodiversity bundle; defaults from pol_input/greendeal/greendeal_scenarios.gms: landscape elements 10% of UAA, organic area 25%, pesticides -50%, mineral fertiliser -20%, nutrient surplus -50%, no diet shift, CAP post-2014. KEY MECHANISM FINDING: conventional_io.gms is invoked with yildReduction='off' - CAPRI applies the pesticide target as an INPUT/COST change plus cover crops, with NO exogenous yield penalty, so replicating it needs no contested agronomic assumption. All five instruments are therefore representable in principle; the landscape-elements one (set_aside_requirement) is now implemented and binding.

set_aside_instrument_bug.note: Attempting the Green Deal scenario-magnitude validation immediately surfaced a silent failure: PolicyScenario.set_aside_requirement was defined and referenced by FOUR scenarios (including SET_ASIDE_10PCT, the Farm-to-Fork landscape-elements equivalent at 10% of UAA) but was NEVER ENFORCED in SupplyModel._build_constraints - whose docstring even listed '5. Set-aside floor if applicable' as intended. Running SET_ASIDE_10PCT returned results BIT-IDENTICAL to the baseline (max relative change 0.00e+00 across 547 cells) while reporting success. FIX: the requirement now binds by shrinking available arable land (arable_avail * (1 - set_aside_requirement)); threaded scenario -> model -> SupplyModule.run -> solve -> _build_constraints. A negative value (a scenario REMOVING set-aside) correctly frees land. VERIFIED: SET_ASIDE_10PCT now moves 547 cells, mean -1.82%, arable crops contracting (to -84% for marginal cells) with reallocation to others (+5.1%). Regression test test_set_aside_requirement_actually_binds added. LESSON: fourth instance of the recurring pattern - an instrument that runs, reports success, and does nothing, caught only by attempting a real validation against an external reference.

policy_instruments_inert_bug.note: Attempting the Green Deal scenario-magnitude validation triggered a systematic sweep of EVERY policy instrument, asking only: does it change the solve? MOST WERE INERT. Until this fix, essentially every CAP scenario in CAPRI-mod returned BASELINE numbers while reporting success. THREE DISTINCT ROOT CAUSES: (1) set_aside_requirement was defined and referenced by four scenarios but never enforced in _build_constraints (its docstring listed it as intended); fixed by binding it to the arable land constraint. (2) CAP ADDERS DISCARDED: the policy module computed them CORRECTLY (BISS -100 moved the wheat adder 265.77->165.77), but model.py wraps them as {'adders': {...}} while _solve_inner iterated the OUTER dict looking for activity codes; 'adders' matched no activity so every adder was thrown away. Note a comment in that same function documents a PREVIOUS version of this exact bug being fixed - it recurred one layer up. (3) nitrate_limit appeared ZERO times in model.py: the constraint was built correctly in the supply solve and the scenario defined the delta, but nothing joined them, so it sat at its non-binding 999999 default. Wired via a NITRATES_DIRECTIVE_N_LIMIT=170 kg N/ha baseline plus the scenario delta. (4) Pillar II (aecs_/anc_/organic_rate_change) and eco-schemes never entered get_supply_policy_adders at all, despite its docstring claiming eco-schemes were included; added, each scaled by the same participation share the payments engine uses (ANC 30%, AECS 20%, organic 8%) so the headline rate is not applied to every hectare. VERIFIED AFTER FIX: biss_rate_change=-100 BINDS (max 5.4e-01), coupled_support BINDS, set_aside=0.10 BINDS (mean -5.26%), nitrate_limit_change=-50 BINDS (-53%) and -120 (-76%, monotonic), aecs/anc/organic all BIND with magnitudes correctly ordered by participation share (ANC 1.25e-01 > AECS 8.37e-02 > organic 3.35e-02), and an UNCHANGED scenario is still a true no-op. milk_quota/sugar_quota exist only as dataclass fields and are implemented nowhere; they now raise NotImplementedError rather than silently returning baseline results (no shipped scenario uses them). Baseline results unaffected - these fixes touch scenarios only. IMPLICATION: the model was well validated on its base year and comparative-static machinery, but the POLICY-RESPONSE layer was largely unconnected. The earlier claim that 'the CAP mechanism is validated' was true only of the payment COMPUTATION (the 58.8bn budget check), not of the supply response to it. Guard test test_policy_instruments_are_not_inert added.

greendeal_scenario_comparison.status: RE-RUN after intensity margin + CAP double-count fixes
greendeal_scenario_comparison.note: First head-to-head scenario-magnitude comparison against CAPRI, now possible because the captrd trajectory and CAPRI's scenario reference share the SAME baseline (verified: SWHE.YILD.2030 = 8515.98 in both). Built GREEN_DEAL_F2F in capri_mod/scenarios (set_aside 0.10 = landscape elements; nitrate delta = nutrient-surplus proxy; organic rate = partial). PARTIAL replication by construction: pesticides -50% and mineral fertiliser -20% are NOT represented (no pesticide input exists in CAPRI-mod; no mineral-N ceiling separate from the nitrate constraint), and organic 25% is a payment RATE here vs an area TARGET in CAPRI. RESULT: CAPRI-mod's response was ~60x TOO STRONG. Mean |change| 69.8% vs CAPRI's 1.17%; SWHE -46.0% vs -1.9%, PULS -72.9% vs -3.6%, SUGB -73.0% vs -0.7%. ISOLATED BY INSTRUMENT: set_aside 0.10 alone gives mean 4.02% (right order vs CAPRI ~1.2%); organic alone 0.02% (negligible); NITRATE alone gives mean 181% and SWHE -75% - the whole over-response is the nitrate constraint. ROOT CAUSE (a real modelling error introduced in the previous session's wiring): the limit was anchored to 170 kg N/ha, the Nitrates Directive figure, which applies to ORGANIC (manure) N only. The constraint acts on TOTAL N from nutrient_coefs, which legitimately exceeds it - FR10 sits at 178 kg N/ha in the BASE YEAR. So at the supposedly-unchanged 170 anchor the constraint was already binding on the base year itself, and any tightening collapsed the solution. PARTIAL FIX APPLIED: the scenario delta is now applied to each region's OWN observed base-year N intensity (SupplyModel.base_n_intensity()), so an unchanged scenario is slack BY CONSTRUCTION. Verified: unchanged control now 0.00% (was already binding before). STILL OPEN: with the anchor fixed, nitrate -10 kg N/ha still gives SWHE -24% vs CAPRI's -1.9%. The supply response to a nitrogen constraint remains roughly an order of magnitude too elastic. Next step is to investigate that elasticity directly - likely candidates are the nutrient coefficients' units/scale and the absence of any intensity-margin (CAPRI can reduce N per ha; CAPRI-mod can only reduce AREA, so the entire adjustment is forced onto the extensive margin, which would systematically overstate the area response).
greendeal_scenario_comparison.diagnosis: INTENSITY-MARGIN HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. capri_data nutrients is a 40x3 frame of FIXED per-activity coefficients (SWHE 125.9 kg N/ha, DWHE 120.4, BARL 101.1 ...). N per hectare is a CONSTANT in CAPRI-mod, so a nitrogen constraint can only be satisfied by cutting AREA. CAPRI adjusts the INTENSITY margin (less N on the same land) and splits the adjustment between intensity and area; CAPRI-mod is forced entirely onto the extensive margin. This is a STRUCTURAL difference, not a parameter error. QUANTIFIED (FR10): base N intensity 178 kg/ha, so a -10 kg N/ha scenario is a -5.6% cut in total N. Area-only adjustment predicts roughly -5.6% area; OBSERVED SWHE response was -24%. So TWO effects stack: (a) the missing intensity margin forces all adjustment onto area, and (b) the constraint falls hardest on N-intensive crops, amplifying the response for wheat well beyond the aggregate cut. FIX SCOPE (not implemented): a genuine intensity margin requires N-per-hectare as a DECISION VARIABLE with a yield-response function, i.e. a structural extension of the PMP problem. The fert module currently derives N FROM yield (_rate_for(crop, nut, yld)) - the dependency runs the wrong way and there is no N->yield response to exploit. This is a real modelling extension, not a parameter tweak, and was deliberately NOT bolted on quickly. IMPLICATION FOR USE: CAPRI-mod's response to AREA-BASED instruments is sound (set-aside 0.10 alone gives mean 4.0% vs CAPRI's ~1.2%, the right order). Its response to INTENSITY-BASED instruments (nitrogen/fertiliser ceilings) is structurally overstated and should NOT be used for policy conclusions until the intensity margin exists.
greendeal_scenario_comparison.rerun_result: Re-ran the Green Deal comparison with both structural defects fixed (nitrogen intensity margin wired; CAP adders passed as a delta so the baseline is no longer inflated). MAGNITUDES: mean |change| 3.16% against CAPRI's 1.17% - a ratio of 2.7x, down from 60x. The order-of-magnitude error is gone and several activities now match closely: SWHE -2.53 vs -1.93, RAPE -1.65 vs -1.31, PULS -5.87 vs -3.57, PIGF +2.07 vs +3.55. STRUCTURE: directional agreement is only 14/28 activities (50%) with correlation +0.031 across all activities, and 5/9 (56%, correlation +0.153) restricted to activities where CAPRI itself moves >1%. So the model now gets the SCALE of a Green Deal response roughly right but does NOT reproduce CAPRI's cross-activity PATTERN. HOW MUCH OF THIS IS EXPECTED: our GREEN_DEAL_F2F is a PARTIAL replication by construction - pesticides -50% and mineral fertiliser -20% are not represented at all, and organic 25% is a payment-rate proxy rather than an area target. Three of five instruments are missing or approximated, and those are exactly the instruments that would drive reallocation BETWEEN crops. Set-aside and the N ceiling mostly shrink everything, so a weak cross-activity pattern is the expected consequence of the missing instruments rather than proof of a further defect. ALSO RELEVANT: 16/28 of CAPRI's own increments are below 0.5%, so much of the cross-activity signal being correlated against is small and a correlation over that set is not very diagnostic. CLEAR DISAGREEMENTS WORTH CHASING: OCER -11.14 vs +2.36, SETA +0.34 vs -5.73, MAIF +0.76 vs +8.13. SETA is notable - CAPRI CUTS set-aside 5.7% under a scenario that mandates 10% non-productive area, which suggests CAPRI books landscape elements in a separate category rather than in SETA, so our set_aside_requirement may not map onto CAPRI's instrument as directly as assumed. HONEST STATUS: magnitude validation has moved from FAIL to roughly-right (2.7x). Cross-activity pattern validation is NOT established and cannot be, on a partial instrument set. Completing the bundle - a mineral-N ceiling distinct from the nitrate constraint, and an organic AREA target - is the prerequisite for a meaningful pattern comparison.

test_harness_and_scope_consolidation.note: STEP 1 - scope locked in. README section 9.0 'Fitness for use' now states plainly what the model is and is not sound for, and the section 9 validation table splits the old blanket 'Policy/CAP: Validated' row into three honest rows: payment COMPUTATION validated (PRME exact, EU budget 58.8bn vs real 55-58bn), AREA-BASED response validated on magnitude (set-aside 4.0% vs CAPRI ~1.2%), INTENSITY-BASED response FAILS (wheat -24% vs -1.9%). The earlier single 'Validated' row was the claim the scenario comparison disproved. STEP 2 - test harness fixed. test_policy_instruments_are_not_inert previously ran one full 248-region solve PER INSTRUMENT and exceeded the time budget even trimmed to 3 regions, which is why it sat unverified for two sessions. Rewritten to test the WIRING rather than run solves: payment instruments are checked by confirming they move get_supply_policy_adders, and a new test_constraint_instruments_reach_the_solve checks set-aside and the N ceiling at the constraint builder. Both now run in seconds and PASS. The constraint test initially failed by indexing the last constraint row for nitrogen; the N row is actually index 3, so the test now locates the moved bound rather than assuming a position (an index-based check silently passes or fails for the wrong reason). FULL SUITE CLEAN RUN (first in three sessions): 32 passed, 1 failed - the failure being the known pre-existing test_market_module_reproduces_its_own_prices at 9/12 within 15%, which fails identically on earlier packaged versions and is a separate world-price matter.

market_price_test_diagnosis.note: test_market_module_reproduces_its_own_prices had failed at 9/12 within 15% for the entire life of the project and had NEVER been diagnosed. Two independent causes, both now fixed. CAUSE A - THE TEST WAS STALE (the actual reason it failed). world_prices.csv had been validated against CAPRI's real PMRK from the capmod base GDX, and nine outliers were CORRECTED: SOYA 292.6->102.7 (the long-flagged 2.85x error), RAPE 321->213, CHES 2581->4815. The test's hardcoded reference dict was never updated, so it was asserting the OLD, KNOWN-WRONG values. The market module was reproducing its inputs perfectly all along (solver returns 213.2 and 102.7 against world_prices.csv's 213.2 and 102.7). References corrected -> 12/12 PASS. LESSON: the failure was read for years as 'the market module disagrees on three commodities'. It was the opposite - the module was right and the test was wrong. A hardcoded reference that is not regenerated from its source silently becomes an assertion about history. CAUSE B - A REAL DATA BUG found while investigating (fixed, independent of the test). Base-year consumption is derived from the trade identity cons = max(1.0, prod - net_exports). Where a region's net exports EXCEEDED its production the raw value went negative and the max(1.0, ...) clamp FABRICATED consumption out of nothing: ROW 'produced' 1094 kt of soy while exporting 123407, and the clamp injected exactly the 122314 kt by which world demand exceeded world supply (verified: injected mass == the gap, to the tonne, for RAPE 22340, SOYA 122314, SWHE 40205). Fixed by raising production to cover net exports so the identity stays feasible. World supply and demand now balance to 0.00% for every commodity (was +21% for oilseeds). ALSO FIXED: real_world SUA overrides replaced individual regions' production AFTER the shares were drawn, so world totals drifted ~27% above the reference (RAPE 91.6 kt against 72 kt). The non-overridden regions are now rescaled to preserve the world total while SUA levels stay exact. NOTE ON A WRONG TURN: I initially blamed the oilseed TRADE FLOWS as ~3x too large, based on real-world trade-share figures. Checking CAPRI's own capmod_trade_flows_2017.csv (105915 rows, already in the repo) showed CAPRI's flows are LARGER still, which falsified that hypothesis and led to the clamp. The data I claimed to need was already present - worth checking before asking.

Zero negative responses across ~690 region-crop checks (0/55-58 regions negative for every crop). Almost certainly fixed as a side effect of the PMP/QP or cross-price work and never retired from the docs. Now pinned by test_no_negative_own_price_elasticities so it cannot silently regress. NOTE: realized elasticities sit ABOVE the calibration targets (PULS realized 1.785 vs target 0.25). That is a separate, real question about calibration fidelity - the SIGN is correct, the MAGNITUDE is not obviously matching PELA - and it is not the same defect as the one documented. #4 DE60 (HAMBURG) NON-CONVERGENCE - NOT PRESENT. nitrogen_intensity_margin.status: WIRED AND WORKING at supply level; a SEPARATE market-loop defect now dominates
nitrogen_intensity_margin.note: Addresses the structural defect found by the Green Deal comparison: nutrient coefficients are FIXED per activity (SWHE 125.9 kg N/ha always), so a nitrogen constraint could only be met by cutting AREA, overstating the response ~10x against CAPRI (wheat -24% vs -1.9%). CAPRI'S MECHANISM (read from supply_model.gms): v_cropNutNeedMultFact is a free VARIABLE scaling each crop's nutrient need, so application per hectare flexes and the model trades fertiliser cost against yield; the adjustment splits between the intensity and extensive margins. IMPLEMENTED (capri_mod/supply/intensity.py): a per-crop intensity factor m in [m_min, 1] scaling N/ha, with a Mitscherlich yield response y(m) = y_base * (1-exp(-k*m))/(1-exp(-k)), normalised so y(1) = 1 EXACTLY - the base year is reproduced by construction, which is what protects PMP calibration when this is switched on. Under a binding ceiling, intensity is cut where revenue lost per kg N saved is LOWEST (not uniformly), so the adjustment falls on low-value crops first. VALIDATED: yield_factor(1.0) == 1.0 to 1e-12; response monotone with diminishing returns; a 20% N cut costs 4.3% yield (agronomically plausible, cf. N-response trials). On FR10 with a real regional ceiling: -0% not binding (intensity exactly 1.000, zero yield loss), -10% -> intensity 0.930 and 1.71% yield loss, -20% -> 0.868 and 3.24%. Previously a 5.6% N cut forced a -24% wheat AREA collapse; now a 20% cut costs 3.2% of yield with area largely intact. THE ONE ASSUMPTION: the curvature k (default 3.0) sets how fast yield falls as N is withdrawn. It is taken from the agronomic literature (k=3 gives ~5% yield loss for a 20% N cut on cereals), exposed as a parameter, and recorded as an assumption - it was NOT tuned to make the CAPRI comparison come out right. A BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING BUILD: the descent loop's iteration budget was (1-m_min)/step, which lets only ONE crop reach the floor; the ceiling was silently left unmet and intensity barely moved (0.992 regardless of the cut). Budget now scales with the number of crops. NOT YET DONE: this is a standalone, tested response function. It is NOT yet called from SupplyModel.solve, so nitrogen scenarios still use the area-only path and the ~10x over-response stands until it is wired in. Wiring it means recomputing net revenues from the intensity-adjusted yields inside the solve, which touches the PMP objective and needs a base-fidelity re-check.
nitrogen_intensity_margin.wiring: WIRED into SupplyModel._solve_inner via _apply_intensity_margin(): when an N ceiling binds it picks the cost-minimising intensity, scales the N coefficients so the constraint sees the reduced application, and scales net revenues by the yield factor so the yield loss is paid for. nutrient_coefs added to the solve's backup/restore block - without it the reduced application leaked into every subsequent solve on the same model. BASE FIDELITY UNCHANGED: 11.35% in real-agriculture cells, identical to before wiring, and 248/248 regions still converge. At full intensity the yield factor is exactly 1.0, so an unbound ceiling is a true no-op - this is the property that makes the extension safe. SUPPLY-LEVEL RESULT (the fix works): a -10 kg N/ha ceiling on FR10 now moves SWHE by -0.1% instead of -24%. Wheat intensity falls to 0.960 (4% less N) for a 0.7% yield loss and the area barely moves - the adjustment sits on the INTENSITY margin, as in CAPRI. Verified two independent paths agree exactly: SupplyModule.run and direct SupplyModel.solve both give SWHE -0.72% across 25 regions. Constraint arithmetic confirmed: N use at base levels falls 104694 -> 98692 against a bound of 98817, so area no longer has to absorb the cut. REMAINING DEFECT, NOT THE INTENSITY MARGIN: at MODEL level the same scenario still gives SWHE -24.25%. Isolated to the MARKET loop - with max_outer_iter=1 it is already -21.61%, so it is the FIRST market pass, not iterative feedback. Supply changes by -0.72% and the market amplifies that into -24%. That is a market-module price-response defect, structurally separate from the nitrogen intensity question, and it will distort ANY scenario that perturbs supply - not just nitrogen ones. It is the next thing to diagnose; the ~60x Green Deal gap cannot be re-measured meaningfully until it is understood.

cap_double_counting_bug.note: Diagnosing why a 0.7% supply change became a 24% model-level response found a bug that had distorted EVERY scenario run through CAPRIModel. Prices barely moved (SWHE +1.0%) and a price rise should RAISE supply, so the amplification was not the market. With price_signals=None on iteration 1 the only difference was the policy dict: adders alone raised wheat +29.05% (1919.4 -> 2477.0) with NO nitrogen constraint; adding the N limit returned it to 1941.8, near the no-policy 1919.4. The '-21.6% nitrogen effect' was the constraint UNDOING an inflated baseline. ROOT CAUSE: calibrated net revenue already contains cap_premium (FR10 SWHE 490.1 of which 322.1 is CAP); get_supply_policy_adders() returns the ABSOLUTE payment (332.2) and _solve_inner ADDS it, nearly doubling CAP support. The same inflation sat in the BASELINE, so scenario-vs-baseline comparisons measured the double-count. FIX: model.py passes adders as a DELTA from the baseline policy, so BASELINE is a no-op and a scenario gets its own change (-100 EUR/ha BISS -> -125.0 on wheat). RESULT: nitrate -10 gives SWHE -0.77% at model level, matching the supply-level -0.72% exactly (was -24.25%); mean activity change 1.06% against CAPRI's ~1.2%. Regression test test_cap_support_not_double_counted added.

greendeal_reference_run_identification.status: the comparison target is probably NOT a full Green Deal run
greendeal_reference_run_identification.note: Re-examining the comparison from the beginning, starting from the SETA anomaly (CAPRI-mod +0.34% vs CAPRI -5.73% under a scenario that MANDATES 10% non-productive area). FINDING 1 - WE HAD THE INSTRUMENT WRONG (fixed). CAPRI's landscape.gms implements the Biodiversity Strategy 10% target as a FLOOR on the non-productive activity: data(ru,'FALL','FLOOR') = lndscpTarg/10 * setAsideTarget * UAAR + SETF. We had implemented it as a REDUCTION of available arable land. Those are different instruments: a floor forces land INTO fallow (SETA rises), whereas shrinking arable squeezes every crop proportionally and leaves SETA untouched. Reimplemented as a SETA floor sized on UAA; SETA now rises +202% for a 10% target (fallow is 2.72% of UAA at base, so roughly a tripling - arithmetically right). FINDING 2 - THE COMPARISON TARGET LOOKS WRONG. With the instrument corrected, CAPRI's own numbers still do not behave like a Green Deal run: (a) mineral fertiliser per UAA (UAAR/NITF) moves only 210.28 -> 208.06, i.e. -1.05%, against an F2F target of -20%; (b) FALL DECREASES 3.79% and SETA -5.73%, when a binding 10%-of-UAA landscape floor must push them UP (10% of UAAR 1111718 is ~111000 against a FALL of only 38943); (c) the whole increment averages 1.17% |change|, very small for a bundle this aggressive. MOST LIKELY EXPLANATION: greendeal_scenarios.gms line 192 encodes the active instruments in the scenario NAME (greendeal_lnds<X>_org<X>_pest<X>_mine<X>_surp<X>_diet<X>_oth<X>), and line 193 renames the all-instruments-off case to 'greendeal_reference'. The uploaded file was renamed to scen_greendeal_2030.txt on extraction, so those settings are lost. The evidence is consistent with the file being a greendeal REFERENCE (instruments off or near-off) rather than the policy scenario - in which case the ~1.17% we have been calibrating against is baseline drift between two reference variants, NOT a Green Deal policy effect. IMPLICATION: the magnitude comparison reported earlier (CAPRI-mod 2.7x CAPRI) may be comparing a real policy shock against a near-null run, which would make the apparent 2.7x meaningless in either direction. This must be resolved before any further calibration against this target. TO RESOLVE: the original CAPRI filename (which encodes lnds/org/pest/mine/surp/diet/oth settings) or the batch/GUI settings of that run. Without it we cannot know which instruments to replicate.

defect_list_items_6_and_8.note: ITEM #8 - HARD-CODED 2017 PATHS (fixed). capri_pmp.py had REGIONAL_FILE and PMP_ELAS_FILE as literal '2017/supply/...' paths. Re-basing the model to another year would have SILENTLY fallen back to the literature defaults - the CAPRI elasticities would simply stop being found, with no error and no warning. Both now go through the loaders' base-year-aware resolve_data_file(), and build_elasticity_table takes a base_year argument. Verified the real sources still resolve: 1543 REGIONAL_CAPRI + 106 PMP_CAPRI cells, unchanged. Pinned by test_elasticity_paths_are_base_year_aware, which asserts both that no year is hard-coded and that the CAPRI sources are still actually found (a path fix that quietly stopped finding the data would otherwise look like a pass). ITEM #6 - ORGANIC AREA TARGET (implemented). Only organic_rate_change existed, a payment RATE - a different instrument from an area TARGET, which is what Farm-to-Fork specifies. Read CAPRI's mechanism from pol_input/greendeal/organic_io.gms: CAPRI does NOT track organic and conventional activities separately; it adjusts the AVERAGE input-output coefficients in proportion to the organic share - DATA(RU, organicCrops, 'Yild', 'percentageChange') = -yildReduction * p_organicAreaTarget(ru). Implemented the same way as SupplyModel.apply_organic_area_target(share): average yield falls by share * ORGANIC_YIELD_GAP and variable cost rises by share * ORGANIC_COST_PREMIUM, with net revenue rebuilt from the adjusted yields and costs so the price and CAP components stay intact. ASSUMED QUANTITIES, exposed as class constants rather than buried: ORGANIC_YIELD_GAP = 0.20 (Seufert et al. 2012 Nature; Ponisio et al. 2015 Proc R Soc B report 19-25%) and ORGANIC_COST_PREMIUM = 0.15. A scenario's organic result depends on these. PLACEMENT BUG FOUND AND FIXED: applying the adjustment in SupplyModule.run() had no effect, because _solve_inner rebuilds net revenues from scratch under a policy shock and overwrote it. Moved inside the solve, after that rebuild. VERIFIED: a 0% target is a bit-exact no-op; a 25% target (= 5% average yield loss) gives a 7.44% mean activity change over real-agriculture cells, with thin-margin crops responding most (PULS -29%, OATS -27%, SWHE -12%) - the expected PMP amplification of a margin change. The headline 'mean 100%' on the first run was near-zero-base cells (COTT and OLIV at base 0.00 showing +1600%), not a real response.

item_5_pesticides.status: UNBLOCKED - a cost-basis PLAP exists; earlier conclusion was too pessimistic
item_5_pesticides.note: ITEM #5 - PESTICIDE INSTRUMENT. Investigated properly rather than assumed. CAPRI'S MECHANISM is replicable in principle: pesticides.gms routes to conventional_io.gms, invoked as '%pestRedu%' 'off' '%pestRedu%' 'on' - i.e. plant-protection input (PLAP) reduced by the target, other costs changed, cover crops on, and yildReduction OFF. So CAPRI applies it as an INPUT/COST change with NO exogenous yield penalty, needing no contested agronomic assumption. WHY WE CANNOT: CAPRI-mod's variable_costs is a SINGLE AGGREGATE per activity (SWHE 701.6 EUR/ha) with no input breakdown, so there is no plant-protection component to reduce. AND THE DATA IS NOT AVAILABLE: capreg_cost_components.csv (105408 rows, 192 regions, 86 activities) itemises CAOF EFUL EGAS ELEC ELUB FERT INPO IRRO REPB REPM SEED TOIN - PLAP is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. INPUT_MANIFEST.json records why: 'PLAP must not be used: in these dumps it duplicates PESTOTAL, a quantity index.' Verified this judgement rather than inheriting it - using PLAP would inject a quantity index into a cost field. The exclusion is correct. WHAT WE CAN BOUND: the itemised components sum to ~62% of TOIN; the unitemised remainder is a median 388 EUR/ha, or 37.8% of total intermediate input, and plant protection sits INSIDE that remainder. That is an upper bound on how large a pesticide cost could be, not a measurement, and splitting it by an assumed share would be exactly the fabrication this project avoids. CONCLUSION: this is a genuine DATA boundary, not a code defect. To implement it we would need a PLAP cost extract from CAPRI's DATA2 in EUR/ha (not the quantity index), or an external plant-protection expenditure series by crop and region. Recorded as out of scope until such data exists, rather than approximated.
