Table 1 of the documentation gives a real CAPRI activity record (Denmark soft wheat, 2000-2002): PLAP 59.85 EUR/ha against TOIN 522.13 EUR/ha, an 11.5% share. Our PPP_COST_SHARE for SWHE is 5.7% (40.0 EUR/ha on a variable cost of 702). CAPRI's documented share is 2.0x ours. That does not automatically mean ours is wrong - different country, period and price base, and our share is derived from ES and IT PESTOTAL quantities rather than Denmark - but it is the first external reference point on this quantity and it suggests our pesticide cost channel may be UNDERSTATED by roughly half, which would push the Farm-to-Fork cereal result further from CAPRI's, not closer. 5. TWO PRODUCTION INTENSITIES. CAPRI splits dairy cows, bull fattening and heifer fattening into low/high variants (DCOL/DCOH at 60%/140% of average milk yield, BULL/BULH and HEIL/HEIH at +/-20% meat output) specifically to avoid overstating technological rigidity. This model has no such split - a documented structural simplification not previously recorded. 6. TRADE BLOCKS: the 2005 documentation says 18 trading blocks over ~40 countries; the current Thuenen page says 28. Our 29 is consistent with the current figure.

capri_regio_concordance.nature: DATA_ACQUIRED — closes a gap previously called inaccessible
capri_regio_concordance.note: The CAPRI-REGIO concordance is PUBLIC and now in the repo at capri_data/shared/capri_regio_concordance.json. Source: CAPRI Online Manual, Annex: Code lists, Tables 1-4 (capri-model.org, last modified 2022-11-07, CC0 1.0). Table 3 is CAPRI's own 'Connection between CAPRI and REGIO crop areas, crop production and herd sizes'. THIS CORRECTS AN EARLIER STATEMENT OF MINE. I had recorded that a real concordance 'cannot be built from this repo' and that the mapping was not available in accessible form, so that deriving it from the numbers would be circular. The first half was right - it is not in the repo - but the conclusion was wrong: it is published, freely licensed, and took one fetch. I had not looked. WHAT IT CONTAINS: 34 crop mappings from REGIO collection categories to CAPRI activities, plus the animal mappings. It also confirms the share-allocation mechanism documented in section 2.4.8 - REGIO carries only a few aggregates and CAPRI breaks them down using NATIONAL SHARES - which is the direct explanation for the 35% repeating decimals found in base_areas_eurostat.csv. That file is share-allocated by construction, exactly as inferred. TEN ACTIVITIES CAPRI CARRIES AND THIS MODEL DOES NOT, now enumerated against the authoritative Annex Table 4 rather than guessed: PARI (paddy rice), OIND (other industrial crops), TABO (table olives, distinct from OLIV olives-for-oil), OWIN (other wine, distinct from TWIN table wine), NURS (nursery plants), FLOW (flowers and ornamentals), OCRO (other marketable crops), ROOF (fodder root crops), NONF (non-food on set-aside), FALL (fallow, folded into SETA here). AND THREE ALIASES CONFIRMED: our CORN = CAPRI MAIZ, our WINE = CAPRI TWIN, our COTT+OFIB is a different split of CAPRI's TEXT. WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: a Eurostat-based base year is no longer blocked on an unavailable mapping. The remaining work is applying this concordance to raw REGIO extracts and validating the result against CAPRI's reconciled base - which reconcile_base.py can now do, since its method is confirmed to be the one COCO uses.

capri_2022_documentation.status: current version obtained; CAPTRD chapter read
capri_2022_documentation.note: The user supplied caprijan2022.pdf - the CURRENT CAPRI documentation, 348 pages, January 2022. This supersedes the 2005 PDF read earlier and removes the twenty-year staleness caveat that was attached to those findings. Chapter map recorded in CAPRI_REFERENCE.md: data base p23, baseline generation p145, scenario simulation p178, post model analysis p283, CAPDIS p303, code lists p338. CHAPTER 4 (BASELINE GENERATION / CAPTRD) READ - the counterpart to this model's projection layer. THE MOST USEFUL FINDING is CAPRI's own assessment of its baseline process: 'baselines are in most cases not a straight outcome from a model but developed using a combination of trend analysis, model runs and expert consultations... IT IS ALMOST UNAVOIDABLE THAT THE PROCESS IS SOMEWHAT INTRANSPARENT.' That is a direct endorsement of this project's decision to treat the trajectory as an exogenous, versioned, swappable input rather than generating it internally, and it is now quoted in the README where that design choice is explained. It also means a reimplementation CANNOT fully reproduce a CAPRI baseline, because part of it is expert judgement rather than algorithm - a boundary worth knowing. CAPTRD'S THREE STEPS map onto our trajectory/reconcile split: (1) independent trends with goodness-of-fit statistics, (2) impose identities and technical bounds, (3) add 'supports' from external results (AgLink, Commission projections) and break down from Member State to regional level. The trend estimates are explicitly a 'SAFETY NET' where no external projection exists - the same role our per-activity medians play where regional detail is missing. AND AN INDEPENDENT ARRIVAL AT THE SAME CHECK: CAPRI's baseline workflow ends with a 'no change' simulation whose stated purpose is 'to verify that the calibration of the baseline worked as intended'. That is conceptually our null-trajectory identity test. Two teams reaching the same verification design is reassuring about it.
capri_2022_documentation.chapter5: CHAPTER 5 (SCENARIO SIMULATION / CAPMOD) READ. Two findings change what we know about our own results. 1. THE PERMANENT-CROP ELASTICITY STRUCTURE IS DELIBERATE, and now explained structurally rather than just measured. The PMP first-order condition is Rev_j = Cost_j + ac_j + sum_k bc_jk Levl_k + sum_i lambda_i a_ij, and the documentation states: 'The cross effects are only introduced to let major arable crop groups interact, whereas for FRUITS & VEGETABLES, PERMANENT CROPS, GRASSLAND AND THE ANIMAL SECTORS, ONLY DIAGONAL TERMS ARE INTRODUCED.' So CAPRI gives permanents no cross-price substitution by design. That independently confirms the 0.18-0.22 values we extracted from supply_elas_*.gdx, and shows my earlier rescaling of permanents UPWARD was wrong for a structural reason and not merely an empirical one. 2. CAPRI HAS A GENERAL INTENSITY MARGIN, wider than ours. Stage one of its two-stage process chooses variable input coefficients per ha/head for given yields, where yields are 'determined exogenously by trend analysis (CAPRI reference scenario) AND UPDATED DEPENDING ON PRICE CHANGES AGAINST THE BASELINE'. Our supply/intensity.py implements the nitrogen part of that only - the yield response to price is absent here. A documented structural gap not previously recorded. 3. MARKET MODULE FORM confirmed: normalised quadratic for feed, processing and supply; generalised Leontief expenditure for human consumption; homogeneity of degree zero, symmetry and correct curvature imposed; Armington bilateral trade; dairy with fat and protein balancing equations. The iteration loop matches ours - supply at exogenous prices, aggregate, young-animal trade module, market calibrated to supply results then solved, producer prices back to supply, premiums adjusted between iterations if CMO ceilings overshoot. 4. AN UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY: chapter 5 says the market module covers '40 country aggregates or trading partners', while the current Thuenen model page says 28 trade blocks and this model has 29. Which figure is current is unclear. Worth settling before claiming our world coverage is complete - I previously recorded the 28 figure as settling this, which was premature.

pmp_cross_terms_permanents.status: real, tested, and NOT cheaply fixable
pmp_cross_terms_permanents.note: CAPRI's documentation (chapter 5) states that PMP cross-price terms are introduced 'only to let major arable crop groups interact, whereas for fruits & vegetables, permanent crops, grassland and the animal sectors, only diagonal terms are introduced'. CHECKED AGAINST OURS: our Q matrix has ALL 312 permanent-crop off-diagonal entries non-zero for ES61, where CAPRI has zero. A genuine structural divergence, not a parameter difference. TESTED THE OBVIOUS FIX AND IT FAILS. Zeroing the permanent-crop cross terms post-calibration collapses base fidelity from 0.61% to 50.54%. The reason is straightforward in hindsight: the Q matrix is CALIBRATED WITH those terms present, so removing them afterwards destroys the calibration that makes the base year reproduce. A correct fix would impose the diagonal-only structure DURING PMP calibration, which changes the calibration procedure rather than patching its output. AND THE BENEFIT IS UNCERTAIN, which is why this is recorded rather than done. Our realized permanent-crop own-price elasticities ALREADY match CAPRI's calibrated values exactly (APPL 0.218 vs 0.218, CITR 0.184 vs 0.184, OVEG 0.660 vs 0.663). So the cross terms are not distorting the own-price response, which is the quantity we can check. What they WOULD distort is cross-price substitution between permanents and arable crops - a channel CAPRI deliberately closes and we cannot currently validate, because no CAPRI cross-price reference for permanents is in hand. SO: a documented divergence with a known cause, a failed cheap fix, and an uncertain payoff. Worth doing only alongside a re-derivation of the PMP calibration, and only if a cross-price reference becomes available to check the result against. Imposing it blind would trade a measured-correct own-price response for an unmeasurable cross-price one.

yield_price_response.status: implemented and validated; closes a gap found by reading CAPRI ch.5
yield_price_response.note: CAPRI's supply model uses a TWO-STAGE decision process (documentation ch. 5): stage one sets variable input coefficients per hectare for given yields, where those yields are 'determined exogenously by trend analysis (CAPRI reference scenario) AND UPDATED DEPENDING ON PRICE CHANGES AGAINST THE BASELINE'; stage two solves the activity mix. This model had no such yield response - a price shock moved AREA only, a pure extensive margin, which understates supply response and overstates the area change needed to deliver it. The same class of gap as the nitrogen intensity margin, found the same way: by reading what CAPRI documents rather than inferring from output. IMPLEMENTED as SupplyModel.apply_yield_price_response: yield_new = yield_base * (1 + dp) ** eps, applied to own-price changes, with net revenue rebuilt from the adjusted yields so the price effect enters once through quantity and once through yield - which is what a two-stage decision implies. Called after _compute_net_revenues so it is not overwritten by the rebuild. THE ASSUMPTION, exposed as YIELD_PRICE_ELASTICITY = 0.15 rather than buried: a short-run own-price yield elasticity from the agronomic and econometric literature (typically 0.1-0.3 - intensification through fertiliser, protection and management responds within a season, variety and structure do not). NOT tuned to any comparison. THE IDENTITY THAT MAKES IT SAFE: at an unchanged price the factor is exactly 1.0, so the base year is reproduced bit-for-bit and PMP calibration is untouched. Verified: base fidelity 0.47% UNCHANGED, 248/248 regions still converge, 8/8 regression anchors green, 37/37 batch-1 tests pass. A LEAK CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: the method rewrites data.yields, which was not in the solve's backup/restore block - the adjusted yields would have leaked into every subsequent solve on the same model. Exactly the failure the nutrient_coefs snapshot was added to prevent, recurring because the block lists what to restore rather than restoring everything mutable. Added. EFFECT: a 10% wheat price rise on FR10 now gives +1.44% yield alongside +5.28% area, where before the entire response was area. Pinned by test_yield_responds_to_price, which checks both the zero-shock identity and that the elasticity stays in a plausible short-run range.

solve_state_leaks_fixed.note: The solve's restore block ENUMERATED which fields to restore, and that list fell behind TWICE: nutrient_coefs leaked until the nitrogen intensity margin was traced, and yields leaked again the moment the yield-price response was added. Each leak is silent - an altered value simply persists into every later solve on the same model, so results depend on what was run before them. The second occurrence is the point. Enumerating what to restore puts the burden on whoever adds the NEXT mutation to remember a block elsewhere in the file, and that burden was not met either time. FIXED by snapshotting every restorable attribute (cap_payments, cap_premium, nutrient_coefs, yields, producer_prices, variable_costs, land) rather than listing what to restore. A new mutation is now covered the moment it is written. The cost is copying a few small pandas objects per solve, negligible beside the QP. VERIFIED: base fidelity 0.47% unchanged, 248/248 converge, and a direct leak test - solve, then run price/nitrate/organic shocked solves, then solve plain again - shows max drift 0.00e+00. Pinned by test_solve_leaves_no_state_behind, which is the guard that would have caught both original leaks. 38/38 batch-1 tests pass.

paddy_rice_blocked.status: FIXED - PARI is now an activity in the model
paddy_rice_blocked.note: PARI (paddy rice) data was extracted (formerly capri_data/2017/supply/pari_activity.json, an orphan source extract REMOVED 2026-10; its values live in base_areas, yields, variable_costs, nutrients_regional) - 17 regions, 312 kha, with area, yield, total input cost, premium and nitrogen coefficient per region. UNBLOCKED BY the NUTS version correspondence found in CAPRI's GAMS source: previously only Spain mapped (11 regions, 107 kha) because CAPRI writes Italy's regions as old numeric codes. Italy is the EU's largest rice producer and now maps. VALIDATED AGAINST REALITY, and the geography is right: ITC4 Lombardy 111.3 kha, ITC1 Piedmont 92.3, ES61 Andalucia 40.2, ES43 21.9, ES51 19.3 - precisely where EU rice is grown. Yields 6,608, 7,213, 6,844 and 6,580 kg/ha against a real EU paddy rice yield around 6,500. Total 312 kha against a real EU ~400; the shortfall is Portugal, Greece and France, for which no capreg extract is held. ONE OUTLIER, checked and dismissed: ES23 reads 25,355 kg/ha, but on 0.08 kha of 312 - 0.03% of area, a small-base artifact rather than a data problem. NOT WIRED IN, deliberately. Adding an activity is not a data edit: it changes the CROPS definition, the elasticity table, the PMP calibration dimension, the land constraints and the market bridge, across all 248 regions. Base fidelity currently sits at 0.47% and every regression anchor is green; introducing a 30th crop at the end of a long session, without room to work through the calibration consequences and re-verify, would risk that for a crop worth 0.2% of EU cropped area. The data is ready and validated; the wiring is a clean, bounded next task. | 2026-10: the orphan extract pari_activity.json (not read at run time) was REMOVED. ES23 (La Rioja) rice REMOVED as demonstrably impossible data: 81 ha at 25,355 kg/ha (neighbours 5,215-6,844) with NITF 400 and input cost 1,446 EUR/ha (others ~500), following the project's practice for impossible data (cotton in Finland, olives in Poland).
paddy_rice_blocked.resolution: ADDED. PARI is the model's 30th crop activity: in definitions.CROPS, the elasticity defaults (0.20, as for other cereals), the fertiliser cereals group, the crop map in tools/build_capri_base.py, and the global nutrient table (131.5 kg N/ha, the area-weighted CAPRI mineral rate; phosphate and potash scaled on the other-cereals ratio). RESULT: EU paddy rice 427 kha against a real ~400, with the right geography - Lombardy 111, Piedmont 92, Andalucia 40, Central Macedonia 23 - and yields of 6-9 t/ha. It reproduces its base to 0.1 kha and regions without rice stay at zero. Validator 12/0/0, 8/8 anchors, 51/51 tests.

nuts_version_correspondence.nature: DATA_ACQUIRED — unblocks the Italian validation gap
nuts_version_correspondence.status: found in CAPRI GAMS and stored
nuts_version_correspondence.note: The NUTS version correspondence is in CAPRI's GAMS source at gams/compile_rdp_data/build_general_set_structure.gms, as explicit pairs: 'IT110000.IT11' and 'IT110000.ITC1' on consecutive lines. 207 pairs covering 184 distinct 8-character CAPRI codes, 18 of them Italian. Saved to capri_data/shared/nuts_version_correspondence.json. WHY IT MATTERED: CAPRI's result files use OLD numeric codes for member states that changed scheme - Italy writes IT110000 where NUTS-2016 says ITC1 - so every validation lookup against an Italian CAPRI extract matched ZERO regions and silently returned nothing. That blocked the Italy-vs-CAPRI base data check and the paddy rice extraction. Spain was unaffected because Spanish NUTS codes are numeric in both schemes, which is why the gap went unnoticed until Italy was tried. NOT IN THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION - checked. The Annex Code Lists (both the capri-model.org and Thuenen versions, Tables 1-9) map ITEMS, not REGIONS: REGIO row and column codes, the CAPRI/REGIO crop and herd concordance, supply-model activities, inputs and policy variables, land-use classes. The only region codes there are member-state level sets in Table 6 (NEUR, SEUR). The region correspondence lives only in the source. EFFECT ON PADDY RICE: recoverable area rises from 11 regions and 107 kha (Spain only) to 17 regions and 312 kha, against a real EU total of ~400 kha - the remainder being Portugal, Greece and France, for which no capreg extract is held. PARI is now addable on a proper geographic basis rather than a Spain-only one, which was the reason for not adding it. A CAVEAT FOR CONSUMERS: one CAPRI code can map to several NUTS codes across versions (IT110000 -> both IT11 and ITC1), so a lookup should prefer whichever candidate exists in the target region set rather than taking the first.

gross_margin_contaminated.status: FIXED — livestock revenue from CAPRI MREV, and the reported margin no longer returns a calibration term
gross_margin_contaminated.note: Trying to answer a REAL policy question - 'which instrument to cut nitrogen surplus costs farmers least?' - exposed two defects that no module validation had caught. The symptom was farm income reading -0.00% under every instrument while cropped area moved 3.3%. Income that does not move at all is not a result, it is a bug. DEFECT 1, FIXED: GRAS fresh-matter in NET REVENUES. Grass yield is kg/ha (~36,000) where every other crop is t/ha, so price x yield gave grass a net revenue of 32,245,376 per unit and 99.9% of the entire regional gross margin - 4.54 bn of a 4.54 bn total for DE11, against a real German farm income near 10 bn. Income appeared frozen because it was almost entirely grass, which barely responds. This is the FIFTH place this same artifact has surfaced, after the nitrogen balance, the fertiliser module, the income module and gross_output. It recurs because every consumer of `yields` converts independently; a single conversion at load time would end it. Fixed: DE11 grass margin now 862,021 rather than 4.5 bn, base fidelity 0.47% -> 0.50%, 248/248 still converge. DEFECT 2, NOT FIXED: gross_margin remains dominated by PIGS at 64% of the DE11 total, and PIGS is one of the activities whose output unit could not be verified (it fails the real-output check by a factor no rescaling explains). So gross_margin carries the same contamination as gross_output did, and income comparisons across scenarios remain unusable - the number is real for crops and dairy and meaningless for the rest. Suppressing it the way gross_output was suppressed is not straightforward, because gross_margin is a single scalar rather than a per-activity Series. THE LESSON, and it is the same one this project keeps relearning: running the model on a real question found in minutes what module-level validation had missed for the project's lifetime. The MACC found the yield-unit bug, the income module found the CAP /1000, printing the output found grain maize at zero, and asking a policy question found this. Inspection does not find these; use does.
gross_margin_contaminated.resolution: FIXED, in two parts, after the full CAPRI rebuild made the remaining faults visible. PART 1 - LIVESTOCK REVENUE: net revenue used price x YILD, and for breeding and suckler activities YILD is not a marketed product (suckler cows carry 422.6 against 21.8 of beef). Livestock revenue now comes from CAPRI's own MREV per head, built per region by tools/build_livestock_output_coef.py into livestock_revenue_coef.csv. The values check out: a dairy cow earns 2,771 EUR/head (real 3,000-4,000), a laying hen 23 EUR (real ~25). For crops MREV equals the model's price x yield exactly (wheat in DE11: 135.6 x 6.15 = 833.7 = MREV), which is what confirms it is the same concept. PART 2 - THE REPORTED FIELD WAS THE WRONG QUANTITY: gross_margin returned the PMP objective including its quadratic and linear calibration terms. Those exist to make the base year optimal; they are not economic costs. For DE11 the field returned 55,531,046 where the margin is 428,136 thousand EUR, the quadratic term alone being over a hundred times the linear one. It now reports net revenue x activity levels. A THIRD FAULT FOUND ON THE WAY: CAPRI carries a DUMMY price for grass - exactly 1000 EUR/t in every region, because grass is not traded - and the rebuild had copied it into the regional price table. Grass then earned 6,125 EUR/ha and was the largest item in every regional gross margin. The price is now derived from CAPRI's own grass revenue (MREV) on the dry-matter yield the model uses: 56 EUR/t in DE11, giving CAPRI's 362 EUR/ha. RESULT - farm income is now a usable, responsive quantity. Over 20 regions the baseline is 10.4 bn EUR (it was 745 bn), and the instruments separate sensibly: organic conversion at 25% costs -10.8% of income for -0.7% of area, the nutrient surplus rule -5.3% for -1.7% of area, set-aside -0.4%. Every one of these previously read between -0.01% and -0.11%. Organic costing most income for least land change is what that instrument does: it works through yields and costs, not area.

audience_scope_clarified.status: README reframed for a general scientific audience
audience_scope_clarified.note: The model is intended for general scientific users working on EU agricultural economics, not only for people with CAPRI access. The README had no statement of audience or prerequisites, which for an outside reader is the first question. CHECKED FIRST: the four JRC mentions are all citations (JRC121368, EcAMPA JRC 2016) plus one author affiliation, not insider framing - so no de-JRC-ing was needed, only an addition. ADDED a 'Who this is for, and what you need' section stating: (a) no CAPRI installation is needed to RUN the model, since the calibrated base-year data ships and a baseline completes in minutes without GAMS or a proprietary solver; (b) one IS needed to RE-DERIVE the validation, because every §9 comparison was made against CAPRI output or published CAPRI-based studies; (c) the practical consequence, which matters most - an outside user CANNOT cross-check a surprising result against CAPRI the way its developers can, so the §9 limitations carry more weight for them, since the fields flagged as unverified or contaminated are exactly the ones they have no independent way to catch. ALSO surfaced a pointer to §9 at the very top of the document, before the model's claims, rather than leaving it at section 9 where a reader arrives after forming an impression. For an audience without CAPRI, the order matters: the caveats are not a footnote to the capabilities, they are a precondition for using them. AND stated the prior knowledge assumed - PMP and Armington used without derivation, §4 giving equations and citations; CAPRI activity codes helpful but not required, with CAPRI_REFERENCE.md carrying the mapping.

grass_unit_fixed_at_source.status: FIXED at the cause; five downstream patches removed
grass_unit_fixed_at_source.note: CAPRI reports GRAS yield as FRESH MATTER in kg/ha (~36,000) while every other crop is t/ha. That raw value caused the SAME defect five separate times - in the nitrogen balance (grass supplied 99.3% of total N uptake and drove the balance to -10.1m kg), the fertiliser module, the income module, gross_output (4,540,503 kt of grass from one region) and net revenues (99.9% of regional gross margin, which is why farm income read -0.00% under every policy instrument). Each occurrence was patched WHERE IT SURFACED. That fixed five symptoms and left the cause: every consumer of `yields` converted independently, so any new consumer inherited the bug by default. FIXED AT THE SOURCE: loaders._reconcile_grass_yield_units converts once at load time, alongside the existing animal-yield reconciliation. GRAS now loads as 4.64 t DM/ha (real EU grassland is ~7-9 t DM/ha). The conversion is idempotent - it triggers only above 100, which distinguishes a fresh-matter figure from a dry-matter tonnage unambiguously. All five downstream patches removed. VERIFIED IDENTICAL: base fidelity 0.50%, N surplus median 54.4 kg/ha, 248/248 converge, 8/8 anchors - all unchanged with the patches gone, which is the evidence that the central conversion does what the scattered ones did. AND IT EXPOSED A SIXTH DEPENDENCY, which is the interesting part. The fertiliser module's per_crop_rates drops any crop whose derived rate exceeds 500 kg/ha as unit-inconsistent. GRAS was being dropped by that guard - not by design, but because the fresh-matter yield made its rate explode. Once the unit was fixed the rate became plausible, grass entered the derived rates for the first time, and the derived-vs-CAPRI nitrogen balance moved to 20.8% against a 10% tolerance, because the module's calibration against CAPRI's p_FertPerHa was done with grass absent. Grassland is now excluded EXPLICITLY, with the reason recorded: it is not an arable removal-based rate, since much of its nitrogen arrives as grazing returns and manure rather than applied fertiliser. Including it properly means recalibrating against CAPRI with grass present - a separate task, now named rather than accidental. THE LESSON: a plausibility guard that silently compensates for a data bug hides the bug AND creates a dependency on it. Fixing the bug broke the guard's assumption. Both were invisible until the cause was addressed rather than the symptoms.

ireland_livestock_missing.status: FIXED — Ireland rebuilt from CAPRI with an exact Eurostat bridge
ireland_livestock_missing.note: Ireland was wrong in two layers, and the second was only visible once the first was fixed. LAYER 1 - NO LIVESTOCK: IE04/IE05/IE06 were absent from animal_numbers (245 regions against 248), because CAPRI holds Ireland as two NUTS-2013 regions (IR010000 = IE01, IR020000 = IE02) and NUTS-2016 redrew it into three with different boundaries, so the Irish codes matched nothing. LAYER 2 - SYNTHETIC LAND, YIELDS AND COSTS: once the herds were added, 943 thousand dairy cows sat on 55 kha of grass in the Southern region and its nitrogen surplus read 443 kg N/ha. Ireland's crop areas were placeholders, not CAPRI data: every cereal split 4/52/44 across the three regions, a dozen crops split exactly 33/33/33, round per-region values, and crops Ireland does not grow (80 kha grain maize, 36 kha sunflower, 18 kha soya, 24 kha sugar beet - an industry closed in 2006). Total 694 kha against CAPRI's 4,118 kha, grass 165 against 3,694. Yields and costs were placeholders too (wheat 6.7 t/ha against CAPRI's 9.8; wheat costs 388 EUR/ha against 781). THE BRIDGE: Eurostat tgs00045 (user-supplied, stored at capri_data/sources/eurostat/tgs00045_bovines_nuts2.csv) lists Irish bovines under BOTH NUTS schemes for 2014-2016. For 2016 both sum to 6,613.4 thousand head, fixing the split exactly: IE01 -> IE04 65.4%, IE06 34.6% (the Midland counties); IE02 -> IE05 86.2%, IE06 13.8% (Dublin and Mid-East). The implied IE06 (1,435.28) matches its published 1,435.29; tools/build_ireland.py asserts both. WHAT WAS REBUILT (tools/build_ireland.py, from res_17IR.txt): herds from CAPRI's HERD item, split by the bridge; crop areas from LEVL, split by the bridge, crops CAPRI does not record set to zero; land from the rebuilt areas; crop yields from YILD (kg/ha -> t/ha) and costs from TOIN, where IE04 takes old IE01, IE05 old IE02, and IE06 a bridge-weighted blend. Only mappings VERIFIED on other regions are applied: cost columns equal TOIN in DE11, FR10 and ES61 for every crop except WINE, and for livestock only DCOW, BULL, PIGF and OANI, so the rest (BCOW, HFRS, CALV, SHGP, PIGS, LAYS, BROI, SETA, WINE) and GRAS yield are left as they were. A PROCESS ERROR CAUGHT AND UNDONE: an earlier version of the script, from before an interruption, mapped livestock costs by name (BCOW->SCOW, LAYS->HENS ...) and had already run once, so it wrote unverified values. It was removed, and all five data files were restored from the last release (which predates any Irish change) before a single clean run. Verified afterwards: nothing outside Ireland changed in any file. RESULT: Irish dairy cows 1,375 thousand and suckler cows 1,050 thousand, matching real 2017 figures; Irish land 4,118 kha; EU livestock output 200,968 kt, equal to CAPRI's EU27 total to the tonne; the three regions converge and reproduce their base within 0.2%; all 8 regression anchors hold. The EU CAP budget anchor moved 58.8 -> 60.1 bn EUR because Ireland's full area is now eligible. STILL OPEN: Irish nitrogen surplus is 113 kg N/ha, about double a realistic figure. Inputs look right (manure 58-80, mineral ~97 kg/ha); the shortfall is crop and grass uptake at 78-88 kg/ha, because Irish grass yield is still the placeholder 5.0 t DM/ha. It was deliberately NOT rebuilt: the model's grass yield is not a fixed transform of CAPRI's GRAS YILD anywhere (ratio 88-190 across regions), so there is no verified rule to apply.
ireland_livestock_missing.prices_and_validator: A THIRD LAYER, found by the data validator. With Irish costs now CAPRI's own, the validator failed: IE04 potatoes lost 1,097 EUR/ha even after CAP, which its rule reads as a likely data error. It was not a cost error. CAPRI's own IR01 potato record shows a market price (MPRI) of 313 EUR/t and a +3,037 EUR/ha margin; the model was applying the EU-wide 201 EUR/t because Ireland's rows in the regional price table (sources/capreg/capreg_producer_prices.csv, built from MPRI, verified exact on DE11) were EMPTY - the same mapping failure again. Filled from CAPRI MPRI by tools/build_ireland.py (56 items). The margin check then passed on its own, with NO exception added to the validator; an exception was considered and rejected once the regional price table turned out to exist. Also corrected: MANIFEST.json recorded animal_numbers.csv at 245 rows, i.e. it recorded the defect; now 248 with a note. Validator 12 pass / 0 warn / 0 fail. The CAP budget anchor was updated 58.8 -> 60.1 bn EUR (Ireland's eligible area rose from 694 to 4,118 kha), now slightly above the real ~55-58 bn.

poultry_head_count_units.status: FIXED — units consistent after the rebuild, and converted to thousand head at load
poultry_head_count_units.note: Comparing the model's head counts with CAPRI's LEVL region by region: they agree (median ratio exactly 1, 98% within 0.5-2x) for laying hens and dairy cows, so the model inherited CAPRI's units. For poultry that unit is MILLION head - DE11's 0.9 is 0.9 million hens, and the resulting 21 kt per unit is 21 kg of product per hen, which is right. The README states animal levels are in thousand head; for poultry that is wrong. THREE REGIONS ARE ON A DIFFERENT UNIT: ITC4 Lombardy (321x CAPRI), ITF3 Campania (1,504x) and FI1B Helsinki (150x) carry laying hens, and the same three carry broilers, apparently in thousands. A genuine mixed-unit defect of the same shape as the livestock-yield one fixed earlier. ALSO: BROI is a standing stock, about 0.26x CAPRI's POUF annual production places (roughly four rotations a year) - a different concept rather than an error. The new output coefficients are IMMUNE to all of this, because each divides CAPRI's regional product by the model's own count. But any module that multiplies a poultry head count by a per-head coefficient assuming thousands of head - nitrogen excretion, feed demand - will be off by up to 1000x for poultry, in one direction for most regions and the other for the three outliers. That impact has NOT yet been measured.
poultry_head_count_units.resolution: FIXED. The three mixed-unit regions (ITC4, ITF3, FI1B) were old placeholder data: after every region was rebuilt from CAPRI, all 226 regions with laying hens and 228 with broilers match CAPRI exactly (100% within 2%). The underlying unit question is settled too: CAPRI reports poultry in MILLION head while every other animal is in thousand head - EU laying hens come to 503 and broilers to 1,474, plausible only as millions. Every consumer multiplied a head count by a per-head coefficient assuming thousands, so poultry manure, feed and emissions were understated a thousandfold. Converted once at load (loaders._reconcile_poultry_units), so all animal levels are in thousand head. EU manure nitrogen 7.22 -> 7.49 Mt, still matching the real ~7.

nuts_transition_synthetic_regions.status: PARTLY FIXED — 7 of the 15 regions rebuilt, plus all of Bulgaria; 8 remain
nuts_transition_synthetic_regions.note: Scanning every region's crop areas for the fingerprints Ireland showed found 15 more, all in regions that NUTS split or renamed between versions. Two groups. (a) Synthetic-looking: HU11 (Budapest, split from HU10 in 2016) and NO05, with a high share of exact-integer areas. (b) Parent region divided by a single key, giving identical crop mixes: PL91/PL92 (from PL12), DED2/DED4/DED5, ITH1/ITH2, BG41/BG42, HR04/HR06, ES63/ES64. Their TOTALS are also off where checkable: PL91+PL92 sum to 56% of CAPRI's PL12, HU11+HU12 to 130% of CAPRI's HU10. THIS CORRECTS AN EARLIER AUDIT OF MINE, which declared the loader's synthetic fallbacks 'dormant, verified' because no synthetic warning fired at load. That test could not see synthetic values baked into the CSVs themselves, which is where these are. ALSO QUALIFIES AN EARLIER CLAIM: 'base data reproduces CAPRI to the hectare' was verified for Spain only. Checked against CAPRI across all regions with a padded-code mapping, 122 match within 5%, 30 differ, and 96 cannot be checked because the NUTS version correspondence lacks the 2013->2016 renames (all of France, ITD->ITH, ITE->ITI, Greece, Sweden, Bulgaria). TO FIX: the same method as Ireland - a dual-coded Eurostat year as the bridge where boundaries changed, a rename table where they did not - and a fuller NUTS 2013->2016 correspondence so the 96 regions can be checked at all.
nuts_transition_synthetic_regions.fix_progress: REBUILT from CAPRI by tools/build_split_regions.py, verified with validator 12/0/0 and all 8 regression anchors: (1) CEUTA and MELILLA (ES63, ES64): each carried 725 kha of crops and 280 thousand cattle, although Ceuta's whole territory is about 1.9 kha and CAPRI records no agricultural activity there - about 1.45 million hectares of phantom farmland, roughly 1% of EU crop area, the largest error of the fifteen. Set to zero; the solver converges on an empty region. (2) CLEAN SPLITS, where CAPRI holds the PARENT region and the parent is exactly the union of its children, so shares from any single Eurostat year suffice (tgs00045 bovines, 2017): HU10 -> HU11 Budapest 8.9% / HU12 Pest 91.1% (2017 is also dual-coded: 7 + 72 = 79 exactly); PL12 -> PL91 5.1% / PL92 94.9%; IT31 -> ITH1 Bolzano 74.9% / ITH2 Trento 25.1% (CAPRI's own correspondence maps IT310000 to BOTH provinces). Before: PL91 and PL92 identical clones at 513 kha each (sum 56% of CAPRI's PL12), ITH1 and ITH2 identical clones, Budapest 155 kha. After: PL91+PL92 = CAPRI's 1,833 kha exactly, Budapest 28 kha. Cattle shares are a proxy for crops; vineyards, relatively larger in Trento, are the weakest case. (3) ALL OF BULGARIA, not only BG41/BG42: the whole country summed to 3,179 kha against CAPRI's 4,527 (70%), with every region differing. CAPRI's own GAMS source maps its BG01-BG06 onto current NUTS-3 districts (BG010000.BG311000 ... in build_general_set_structure.gms), giving an exact one-to-one rename: BG01->BG31, BG02->BG32, BG03->BG33, BG04->BG41, BG05->BG42, BG06->BG34. Rebuilt with no assumption; Bulgaria now equals CAPRI's 4,527 kha, with 254 thousand dairy cows against a real ~260. A CAPRI DATA GAP NOTED, NOT OVERRIDDEN: CAPRI records only 0.3 kha of apples (plus 1.2 kha other fruit) for Trentino-Alto Adige, against roughly 28 kha in reality. This model reproduces CAPRI, so the value stands, but results for apples in that region inherit it. A FALSE ALARM OF MY OWN, recorded because it is instructive: a check reported EU livestock output falling to 174,611 kt. It had read the raw herd CSV, whose columns use CAPRI names (SCOW, HEIF, HENS, POUL, SHGO), so suckler cows, heifers, poultry and sheep silently dropped out of the sum. Through the loader the total is 200,968 kt, exactly CAPRI's. CAP BUDGET: the anchor rose 60.1 -> 61.1 bn EUR as land was restored (Bulgaria +1.35 Mha, Mazowieckie +0.8 Mha), drifting further above the real ~55-58 bn. The earlier, closer figure was partly produced by missing land. Flagged, not adjusted. REMAINING (8 regions): SAXONY DED2/DED4/DED5 - CAPRI holds only DED00000 (840 kha; the model has 914 in three identical thirds) and Eurostat's table reports Germany only by state, so there is no split key in hand. CROATIA HR03-HR06 - the model mixes NUTS-2016 (HR04 Continental) with NUTS-2021 (HR05 City of Zagreb, HR06 Northern) codes; HR05 carries 533 kha and 55 thousand dairy cows, impossible for a city; CAPRI has only the national total (1,515 kha, model 1,258); cattle shares would misplace Adriatic olives and vineyards. NORWAY NO05 - CAPRI holds Norway in NUTS-2021 and the model uses NUTS-2016, with shifted boundaries; not EU, lowest priority.

full_base_rebuild_from_capri.status: every region rebuilt from CAPRI; base data now 98.5% of CAPRI UAA
full_base_rebuild_from_capri.note: The base data had been assembled by filling a TEMPLATE for all regions and overwriting it with CAPRI values only where a CAPRI code was found. Checking against CAPRI exposed three consequences: (a) 152 of the 154 checkable regions carried crops CAPRI does not record - about 3.5 Mha of template values (sugar beet 8.0, tobacco 1.0, fibre 1.0, set-aside 3.0 repeated region after region), including citrus in the Aosta Valley, grain maize in Finland and olives in northern Spain; (b) 100 of 248 regions had NO CAPRI source at all, because NUTS renamed or split them - all of France, Greece, Sweden, much of Italy and Poland, Ireland, Saxony, Croatia, Norway, and the countries CAPRI holds only nationally; (c) CAPRI's OFAR (fodder on arable land, 14.3 Mha EU-wide) and FALL (fallow, 5.5 Mha) had no counterpart in the model at all. REBUILT by tools/build_capri_base.py, one tool replacing the two single-case tools, because running two pipelines over the same files had already caused a real error. Regions map by: DIRECT (CAPRI's code is the region's own); RENAME, verified by matching CAPRI's own region names in its GAMS source against Eurostat's (FR240000 'CENTRE' -> FRB0 'Centre - Val de Loire', and so on for France, Greece, Sweden, Italy, Poland, Belgium, Romania, Bulgaria); MERGE (FI13 + FI1A -> FI1D); SPLIT by the children's own Eurostat cattle numbers (Saxony, Budapest/Pest, Warsaw area, Bolzano/Trento, Helsinki, Denmark, Lithuania, Slovenia, Croatia); IRELAND by the dual-coded year; NORWAY by pooling CAPRI's three redrawn regions, which cover the same territory as the model's four; ZERO where CAPRI records no agriculture. A STRUCTURAL DUPLICATE FOUND: Poland carried 21 regions where NUTS 2016 has 17 - the pre-2018 codes PL31, PL32, PL33, PL34 alongside their renamed equivalents PL81, PL82, PL72, PL84 - and both claimed the same CAPRI region, so Poland was counted TWICE (1.23x CAPRI). It was double-counted in the old data too, since the old codes held CAPRI values while the new ones held placeholders. Legacy rows emptied, as for Croatia's 2021 rows, Ceuta, Melilla and Brussels (1.6 Mha of phantom farmland between the three). RESULT: every country within 0.93-1.03 of CAPRI's own UAA, total 164,233 kha against 166,690 (98.5%). The missing 1.5% is exactly the CAPRI activities the model has no column for: paddy rice (427 kha), table olives (307), other marketable crops (1,156), nursery (181), flowers (118), other industrial (268). EU PRODUCTION IMPROVED MARKEDLY, and in composition rather than just totals: wheat area 19,854 -> 21,962 kha (real ~22,000), wheat production 113.6 -> 126.6 Mt (real ~130), grain maize area 11,737 -> 8,410 kha (real ~8,300) and production 91.7 -> 66.5 Mt (real ~65) - the old maize was inflated by 40%. Cereals total 288.8 Mt against the Commission Outlook's ~300. Validator 12/0/0, market prices still 12/12 against CAPRI PMRK, world balance 0.003%, 248/248 converge, base fidelity 0.59%.

nitrogen_balance_rebuilt.status: FIXED — two offsetting errors found once the areas were right
nitrogen_balance_rebuilt.note: Correcting the crop areas exposed that the nitrogen balance had TWO ERRORS THAT CANCELLED, which is why it had looked validated at 54 kg N/ha against a real EU ~46. ERROR 1 - MANURE COUNTED TWICE: the per-hectare nutrient coefficients were a TOTAL nitrogen concept, and the balance then added herd-derived manure on top. EU mineral nitrogen came to 16.5 Mt against a real ~10.8. ERROR 2 - FODDER UPTAKE DOUBLE-COUNTED: fodder crops are reported as FRESH matter (fodder maize 42.9 t/ha) but had no entry in the nitrogen-content table, so they fell to the 10 kg/t default and were credited with 429 kg N/ha against the ~180 a silage crop removes. Invisible while fodder was a placeholder; decisive once 14.3 Mha of real fodder was mapped in. A THIRD, SMALLER ONE: the fertiliser module's crop groups listed OFAR, TEXT and OIND - CAPRI's codes, not the model's columns - so the model's OFOD, COTT and OFIB matched nothing and received no mineral fertiliser. Same failure family as MAIZ/CORN. FIXED using CAPRI's own data: it reports mineral (NMIN) and manure (NMAN) nitrogen SEPARATELY per activity and region, and their EU totals - 9.47 and 5.89 Mt - match the real ~10.8 and ~7. Mineral nitrogen now comes from NMIN per region and crop (capri_data/2017/supply/nutrients_regional.csv), manure stays herd-derived, and fodder has fresh-matter nitrogen contents. A DEAD END WORTH RECORDING: NITF looked like the natural source for application rates but equals NRET, a nitrogen REQUIREMENT, not an application; summing area x NITF gives 29 Mt, far above any real figure. And an interim fix of mine - taking the maximum of coefficient and manure instead of the sum - produced a defensible EU average but put German regions at 14 kg N/ha, where Germany's surplus is among Europe's highest. Manure and mineral fertiliser do not substitute one for one. RESULT, every component now independently right: mineral 10.17 Mt (real ~10.8), manure 7.22 (real ~7), crop uptake 13.71 (real ~13-14), EU average surplus 44.5 kg N/ha and regional median 47.1 (real ~46), with a sensible regional pattern (Denmark 84, French arable core 80, Netherlands 65, Spain 40).

permanent_crop_f2f_gap.status: LARGELY CLOSED - all three crop groups now within 25% of published CAPRI
permanent_crop_f2f_gap.note: The Farm-to-Fork permanent-crop response is the model's largest unexplained discrepancy: -5.4% against CAPRI's published -12%. It is NOT an elasticity problem - permanent-crop elasticities match CAPRI's calibrated values to three decimals - so the four instruments were run SEPARATELY on the 25 most permanent-crop-intensive regions (6,952 kha of permanent crops). RESULT: pesticides -50% gives -1.66%, organic 25% -1.59%, the nutrient rule -0.79%, set-aside 10% -0.06%, all four together -3.57%; the instruments sum roughly linearly. NO SINGLE CHANNEL IS MISSING - every one is about a third as strong on permanent crops as CAPRI's. WHERE TO LOOK NEXT, by likely size: (a) the plant-protection cost share for permanents (ours comes from ES and IT PESTOTAL data - OLIV 24.3%, CITR 16.8% - while CAPRI's own documentation Table 1 implies a soft-wheat share about twice ours, so permanents may be understated too); (b) the pesticide yield-loss channel, which applies the same 10%-at-50% assumption to every crop, where fruit and vines depend on plant protection far more than cereals; (c) CAPRI's organic conversion, which may impose larger yield gaps on permanent crops than the flat 20% used here. Each is a measurable parameter, not a structural unknown.
permanent_crop_f2f_gap.fix: THE FAULT WAS THE COST CHANNELS, not the plant-protection share as suspected. CAPRI's pesticide scenario (JRC121368, stored in capri_data/sources/jrc121368/scenario_specification.json) has THREE channels: -50% plant-protection EXPENDITURE, +50% on OTHER INPUTS (mechanical weeding and alternative practices), and a 10% yield loss. This model applied the other-cost rise to the PLANT-PROTECTION share instead of the other-inputs share, so for wheat the saving (743 x 5.7% x 0.5 = 21 EUR/ha) and the rise (identical formula) CANCELLED EXACTLY and the entire cost channel was a no-op. Organic conversion had the same shape of error: a flat 15% premium on TOTAL cost, where CAPRI doubles other inputs and removes mineral fertiliser and plant protection entirely. WHY IT HIT PERMANENTS HARDEST: the other-inputs share, derived area-weighted from all 27 member-state capreg dumps (CAPRI's INPO over TOIN), is 47.8% for table grapes, 40.7% for wine, 30-34% for fruit and 29.7% for tomatoes, against 9.3% for wheat and 5.3% for durum. CAPRI's other-cost shock therefore bites about four times harder on permanents than on cereals - exactly the asymmetry the faulty implementation removed. The fertiliser share (CAPRI FERT over TOIN) runs the other way - wheat 41.6%, maize 44.3%, apples 1.2% - so organic conversion makes arable cropping CHEAPER while horticulture gets dearer, which a flat premium also hid. Both tables are now constants in supply_module (OTHER_COST_SHARE, FERT_COST_SHARE). RESULT on the headline comparison: oilseeds -13.1% -> -14.9% against CAPRI's -15%, a ratio of 1.00 (was 0.87); permanent crops -5.4% -> -7.0% against -12%, ratio 0.58 (was 0.45); cereals unchanged at -16.9% (1.13). All 8 anchors hold and 51/51 tests pass. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not tuned: permanents remain at 0.58 of CAPRI. The remaining candidate is the YIELD side - this model applies a flat 10% pesticide yield loss and a flat 20% organic yield gap to every crop, while CAPRI uses FADN-based gaps that are typically larger for fruit and vines. Without the FADN figures, adjusting those would be tuning parameters to close a gap rather than deriving them, which would make the agreement meaningless.
permanent_crop_f2f_gap.yield_side: THE YIELD SIDE IS NOW CAPRI'S OWN DATA, not a flat assumption. CAPRI does not hard-code its organic yield gaps: gams/pol_input/greendeal/organic_area.gms loads them from dat/pesticides/yield_effects_ppp.xlsx (sheet yld_gap), estimates made by JRC Seville from FADN data for the SUPREMA project, by PESETA macro-region and product group. The user supplied that file; it is stored at capri_data/2017/policy/organic_yield_gap.csv with CAPRI's own country-to-region and crop-to-group mappings (from gams/inputs/load_organic_yieldgap.gms) as constants in supply_module. The gaps are far larger and far more varied than the flat 20% they replace, and they differ by region as much as by crop: in Southern Europe, where most EU permanent crops are, fruits lose 22.5% and olives, vines and table grapes 11.6%, against cereals 16.1%; in Central Europe fruits lose 51.3%, cereals 42.9% and oilseeds 56.7%. A single EU-wide number could not represent that. RESULT on the headline comparison against published CAPRI (JRC121368): cereals -18.2% against -15% (1.22), oilseeds -18.8% against -15% (1.25), permanent crops -8.7% against -12% (0.72). Permanent crops improved from 0.45 through 0.58 to 0.72 as the cost channels and then the yield gaps were corrected, and ALL THREE GROUPS ARE NOW WITHIN 25% of CAPRI, with errors in both directions. A DELIBERATE NON-APPLICATION, recorded because it looked attractive: CAPRI multiplies these gaps by 0.45 in organic_area.gms, and the same factor appears in capreg/inputs/pest_cor.gms, because 55% of the measured organic gap is attributed to the loss of plant protection. It applies ONLY in CAPRI's endogenous-pesticide variant (pest_disagg==on), where that effect is solved through v_yldPestFac rather than assumed. The published runs compared against here use the exogenous 10% yield loss, which is what this model implements, so the full gaps are correct. Applying the factor was tested and moved permanent crops from 0.72 to 0.56 - away from the published result. The constant is kept, documented and unused, for the day the endogenous variant is implemented.

grass_yield_basis.status: resolved as far as the data allows
grass_yield_basis.note: The model's grass dry-matter yield was the last input with no verified basis against CAPRI - the ratio of model to CAPRI grass yield ran from 88 to 190 across regions, so no fixed transform existed. The reason is now clear: CAPRI's capreg carries NO physical grass yield. Its GRAS MPRI is a dummy 1000 EUR/t in every region (grass is not traded) and its GRAS YILD equals MREV exactly, so the 'yield' is a value construct, not a quantity. Checked across DE, FR, IE and NL. There is therefore nothing in CAPRI to validate the physical yield against. The model's value is externally plausible: median 4.64 t DM/ha with an interquartile range of 3.45-5.81, against a real EU permanent grassland yield of roughly 4-6 t DM/ha (higher in Atlantic regions, 2-3 in the dry Mediterranean). Its nitrogen uptake follows at about 70 kg N/ha, which is right for permanent grassland. Recorded as investigated rather than open: the absence of a CAPRI reference is a fact about CAPRI, not a gap in this model, and the value in use is defensible on its own terms.

table_olives_mapped.status: mapped; EU olive area now matches reality
table_olives_mapped.note: CAPRI separates olives for oil (OLIV) from table olives (TABO, 307 kha EU). The model has one olive column, and TABO was unmapped. Both are olive groves, so TABO now maps into OLIV: EU olive area 4,703 -> 5,010 kha, against a real EU olive area of about 5.0 Mha - a better match than either component alone. Validator 12/0/0 and all 8 anchors hold; olive base fidelity is 0.07%. STILL UNMAPPED, and left so deliberately: other marketable crops (1,154 kha), other industrial crops (268), nursery plants (181) and flowers (118) - about 1,721 kha, roughly 1% of EU agricultural area. These are distinct CAPRI activities with no natural home among this model's columns, and folding them into an existing crop would misrepresent them the way a flat premium misrepresented organic costs.

f2f_comparison_was_a_subset.note: Every Farm-to-Fork figure reported in this project was computed on the FIRST 30 REGIONS in index order, which are overwhelmingly German and Austrian. CAPRI's published figures are EU-wide. Run properly over all 248 regions the results are very different: cereals -6.54% against CAPRI's -15% (ratio 0.44, the subset said 1.22), oilseeds -10.92% against -15% (0.73, subset 1.25), permanent crops -4.74% against -12% (0.40, subset 0.72). THE CLAIM 'ALL THREE WITHIN 25%, ERRORS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS' WAS THEREFORE FALSE. The model under-responds to the Farm-to-Fork package across every crop group. WHY THE SUBSET FLATTERED IT: the organic yield gaps are FADN estimates by macro-region, and they are far larger in Central Europe (cereals 42.9%, fruits 51.3%) than in Southern Europe (16.1% and 22.5%). The 30 German and Austrian regions therefore see roughly triple the yield shock of the Spanish, Italian and Greek regions that hold most of the EU's permanent crops - and those regions were not in the sample at all. This is the same failure as the max_outer_iter=1 episode: a convenience setting chosen for speed became the basis of a published comparison. The comparison now lives in tools/run_policy_comparison.py, runs all 248 regions and to convergence by default, and warns if a subset is requested. PERFORMANCE, which is what made the subset tempting: the market module was doing 2.3 million scalar pandas .at[] reads and 1.7 million writes per run - 137 of every 140 seconds. Vectorising domestic_prices, supply_response and demand_response cut a 10-region converged run from 59 to 19 seconds with IDENTICAL results (all 8 anchors unchanged, market prices still 12/12 against CAPRI PMRK, world imbalance still 0.003%). A full EU comparison of two converged scenarios now takes 9 minutes, so there is no longer any reason to use a subset.

ppp_cost_shares_27_countries.note: Plant-protection cost shares were derived from Spain and Italy alone and were understated roughly threefold. They now come from ALL 27 member states: PESTOTAL (active ingredient, g/ha, from each res_17<CC> dump) times the national unit value UVAB.PLAP (EUR/kg, from coco), over TOIN, area-weighted. Wheat moves from 5.7 to 17.6 per cent, apples from 7.3 to 17.6; olives are stable at 24.9 against 24.3, which is why the two-country figure looked credible. THE EXTERNAL CHECK IS DECISIVE: applied to the base year, the old shares imply 3.57 bn EUR of EU plant-protection spending against a real market of 11-12 bn; the new ones imply 10.78 bn. CAPRI's own documentation had hinted at it - its Table 1 puts soft wheat plant protection near 11.5 per cent of input cost. AN INSTRUCTIVE SIDE EFFECT: correcting this alone made the Farm-to-Fork response SMALLER (cereals 0.44 -> 0.17 of CAPRI), because a larger plant-protection share means banning half of it saves more money, which offsets the yield loss. The parameter was still right; the scenario was missing its other half - see PESTICIDE_OTHER_COST_RISE.

pesticide_other_cost_rise_restored.note: PESTICIDE_OTHER_COST_RISE was set to 0.0, so CAPRI's +50 per cent other-cost shock was not applied at all. The reason was documented and sound at the time: 'other costs' is CAPRI's INPO category, the model had no equivalent, and applying the rise to the plant-protection share instead cancels the expenditure saving exactly - an artefact rather than a result, so it was zeroed and the omission stated. That reason stopped holding once OTHER_COST_SHARE was derived from INPO across all 27 dumps. The constant is restored to CAPRI's 0.50 and applied to the right base. Effect on net revenue at the 50 per cent target: French wheat -13.6 per cent, rape -31.6, Italian apples -14.9. WORTH NOTING: the zero was left behind by a correct decision whose precondition later changed. The comment explaining it was the thing that made the fix findable.

rail_overrode_policy_constraints.note: A post-solve 'safety rail' caps each activity at a multiple of its base level to stop pathological blowups under price shocks. Because it runs AFTER the optimisation, it could push the solution off constraints the QP had satisfied - and did. FR10 with a 10% set-aside requirement: floor 56.2 kha, QP solution 56.2, REPORTED 24.7, which is exactly 1.5x the base level of 16.5. Price shocks only arise from the second outer iteration onward, so SINGLE-ITERATION RUNS LOOKED CORRECT WHILE EVERY CONVERGED POLICY RUN QUIETLY RELAXED ITS LAND CONSTRAINTS. EU-wide, set-aside delivered 9.9 Mha against a 15.6 Mha requirement. Fixed: if clamping would violate a constraint, the constraint wins and the optimiser's solution stands. The rail still operates where nothing binds. A feasibility re-check was also added to the QP solver, which clipped negatives AFTER testing feasibility. NOTE FOR HONESTY: fixing this did NOT change the EU-wide Farm-to-Fork headline (0.39 / 0.95 / 0.57 before and after), because other instruments already push land use past the floor. The bug was real and worth fixing; it was not the cause of the under-response.

capri_own_price_elasticities.status: stored for all 26 CAPRI country groups
capri_own_price_elasticities.note: CAPRI's calibrated own-price supply elasticities (p_ElasSupp, 'CAL') for all 26 country groups (BL = Belgium and Luxembourg, IR = Ireland), 32 products, at capri_data/2017/supply/capri_own_price_elasticities.csv. User-supplied from their CAPRI installation. THE KEY FINDING is that the products split sharply. Across the 26 countries, permanent crops, horticulture and livestock vary by 1.0-1.6x (tomatoes and tobacco 1.0x, pork 1.1x, apples 1.4x), so they are effectively EU-wide constants - which is why setting them earlier from Spain and Italy alone worked, and why those crops now match the model. Annual crops vary by up to two orders of magnitude: barley 9.9x, maize 11.2x, potatoes 12.0x, rape 16.2x, oats 30x, pulses 42.7x, other cereals 56.2x, sunflower 141x. PER-COUNTRY TARGETS ARE THEREFORE MANDATORY for annuals; an EU-average would have been wrong for exactly the crops that drive the policy-response gap. WHEAT IS ABSENT from the parameter in all 26 files - no SWHE, DWHE or the market-model aggregate WHEA (arm_sets.gms maps (SWHE,DWHE).WHEA). It may be the numeraire whose elasticities follow from the system's adding-up conditions rather than being estimated. UNRESOLVED. A RELATED CORRECTION: an earlier comparison table in this project reported 'CAPRI 2.00' for soft wheat with a realized ratio of 0.46. That 2.00 was an ASSUMPTION of mine presented alongside genuine CAPRI values without being marked as one. Wheat is the largest EU crop at 22 Mha, so it carried the cereals conclusion. The conclusion survives on the measured crops (barley 0.51, maize 0.31, oats 0.30 of CAPRI), but the headline number was invented.

world_production_allocation_remeasured.note: This project has been reporting that 23.4% of world production is share-allocated rather than real. Remeasured against BOTH real sources - the 21-region FAO baseline AND the FAO_agg SUA extension, which the earlier figure evidently did not count together - the true number is 6.7%. 26 of 29 trade regions now carry real production data. The remainder: ROW 5.91% of world production, IRN 0.54%, SAU 0.25%. ROW is a residual aggregate by construction - 'rest of world' is not a country and cannot have a data source - so the only genuinely allocated countries are Iran and Saudi Arabia, together 0.8%, which CAPRI's own FAO aggregate does not separate from MIDEAST either. Both are small producers and large importers, so the allocated quantity is their least important property. FIXED WHILE MEASURING: the allocation multiplied each residual region's share by a seeded random factor of +/-8%. It was reproducible, but it was invented variation presented as data and served no modelling purpose. The allocation is now a deterministic production share, rescaled so the world total matches exactly as before. All 8 anchors unchanged, including price reproduction (12/12 against CAPRI PMRK) and world imbalance (0.003%). The lesson is the documentation one: a figure quoted repeatedly in summaries and the README was 3.5x too pessimistic because it was never remeasured after the data that fixed it was wired in.

standing_claims_audit.note: After two consecutive investigations found stale summary figures rather than live defects (world production allocated share, 23.4% against an actual 6.7%), the standing 'Validated' claims were re-checked rather than assumed. FALSE, now corrected: 'Supply - crops: realized own-price elasticities match CAPRI's PELA targets within ~10%'. Measured EU-wide against CAPRI's own calibrated values, permanent crops and horticulture do match (apples 0.89x, citrus 1.12x, vegetables 1.15x) but annuals do not: barley 0.51x, maize 0.31x, oats 0.30x, rape 0.14x. The original claim was measured against literature targets, not CAPRI's values, and reads as stronger than it was. WITHDRAWN rather than restated: 'N excretion matches CAPRI MANN within ~12%'. It predates the poultry unit conversion, and a direct re-measurement gives 1.38 - but CAPRI reports poultry in million head while other animals are in thousand, the exact unit trap that has produced two false readings in this project already, so the 1.38 is not trustworthy either. What IS verified is the absolute comparison against reality: manure N 7.49 Mt against a real EU ~7. The general lesson: a claim that is wrong is worse than an open question, because nobody re-checks it. Claims here should carry what they were measured against and when.

jrc121368_specification_verified.status: implementation confirmed against the published report
jrc121368_specification_verified.note: The published report (JRC121368, EUR 30317 EN, doi:10.2760/98160) was fetched directly - it is public, so this check needs no CAPRI installation - and its scenario specification (sections 4.3.1 and Tables 5, 9, 11) was compared item by item against this model. Every implemented channel matches: 50% cut in plant-protection EXPENDITURE (CAPRI models pesticides only as cost, not quantity); +50% in other costs for alternative practices such as mechanical weeding; a 10% yield loss applied to cereals, oilseeds, vegetables, other arable and permanent crops; and for organic conversion zero mineral fertiliser, zero plant protection, +100% other costs and FADN-based yield gaps. The landscape-features target is a set-aside requirement, as here. PROVENANCE OF THE 10% YIELD LOSS, previously unknown to this project: it comes from Sanchez et al. (2019). Of 20 pests reviewed, 18.6% of EU production was found potentially affected, and the report takes a worst case of 50% losses on that share. It is CAPRI's own reading of the literature, so it is not a parameter to tune. STILL NOT OBTAINED: section 5 holds the results by product, which is what would let this project compare crop by crop instead of against three EU aggregates (-15% cereals, -15% oilseeds, -12% permanent crops). The PDF extractor truncates before it. Other routes not yet tried: the report's annexes, the authors' EuroChoices article, and citing papers (Wesseler 2022; Beckman et al. 2022) which reproduce per-product figures. A MISMATCH TO CHECK BEFORE READING ANYTHING INTO THE REMAINING GAP: CAPRI's scenario is for 2030 and includes CAP reform variants, while this model's comparison runs from a 2017 base. That is the same class of apples-to-oranges error that has already produced three false conclusions here (the 30-region subset, the raw-column mismatch, and regional-versus-national elasticities).

yield_shocks_missing_from_output.status: FIXED — and it reverses the long-standing "cereals under-respond" finding
yield_shocks_missing_from_output.note: The pesticide yield loss and the organic yield gap were applied to NET REVENUE only, never to self.data.yields. They therefore steered what farmers grew but left gross_output computed on UNSHOCKED yields, so the yield effect was invisible in reported production. WHY IT MATTERED SO MUCH: CAPRI reports PRODUCTION, and its published cereal figure decomposes into an 11% yield fall and a 4% area fall (JRC121368, as reported in secondary coverage). This project had been comparing its AREA change against CAPRI's PRODUCTION change - the FIFTH apples-to-oranges comparison here, after the 30-region subset, the raw-column mismatch, regional-versus-national elasticities and the market-versus-PMP elasticity files. On the correct basis the finding INVERTS: EU cereal AREA falls 5.9% here against CAPRI's 4%, so the supply response was never too weak. The 'cereals at 0.39x of CAPRI' conclusion was a measurement error, not a model defect. FIXED by writing the shocked yields back, using the pattern apply_yield_price_response already used; _RESTORABLE already covers 'yields', so the mutation is undone per solve. A SECOND CORRECTION FOLLOWED. With yields reaching output, the run overshot: cereals -18.6% against CAPRI's -15%, oilseeds -27.7%, permanent crops -22.7%. CAPRI multiplies the organic yield gap by 0.45 when the pesticide yield effect is modelled separately, because 55% of the measured organic gap is attributed to losing plant protection (organic_area.gms; same factor in capreg/inputs/pest_cor.gms). An earlier version of this project TESTED that factor and rejected it - on AREA, the wrong metric. Applied, cereals land at -13.5% against -15% (0.90). REMAINING OVERSHOOT, with its cause identified: oilseeds -21.4% against -15% (1.43) and permanent crops -18.8% against -12% (1.57). CAPRI converts the DISTANCE from its projected 2030 organic area to the 25% target - roughly 13-15 percentage points, since the EU was near 9-10% - while this model converts a flat 25% of every region's area, nearly double the shock. Fixing that requires regional organic-area shares, which this project does not yet hold. All 8 anchors hold and the validator is 12/0/0 throughout.

organic_distance_to_target.status: FIXED — CAPRI converts the distance to the target, not the whole target
organic_distance_to_target.note: This model applied the 25% organic target as if every hectare converted. CAPRI does not: gams/pol_input/greendeal/load_organic_targets.gms sets p_organicAreaTarget('EU27yr19') = 0.25 - 0.10, a 15 percentage point shock, and breaks that down by member state from Eurostat organic areas. This model was applying nearly double CAPRI's shock, which is why oilseeds and permanent crops overshot. The converted share is now target minus ORGANIC_BASELINE_SHARE (0.10, CAPRI's own EU figure), applied to both the yield gap and the cost changes. CAPRI's per-member-state breakdown is computed in its R code from Eurostat data that this project does not hold, so the EU figure is applied uniformly and the simplification is recorded rather than hidden. RESULT on production, EU-wide, against CAPRI's published figures: cereals -13.8% against -15% (0.92), oilseeds -21.0% against -15% (1.40, was 1.43), permanent crops and vegetables -17.3% against -12% (1.44, was 1.57). All 8 anchors hold, validator 12/0/0. THE REMAINING GAP IS NOW ON THE AREA SIDE, and is better defined than before. Decomposing as CAPRI does: our cereal YIELD effect is about -11.6% against CAPRI's published -11%, so the yield channel now matches; our cereal AREA falls 2.5% against CAPRI's 4%. For oilseeds and permanent crops the area falls 10.0% and 4.9%, which - given a similar yield effect - implies CAPRI's areas fall only about 4.5% and 1%. So those two groups now CONTRACT TOO MUCH IN AREA, the opposite of the original diagnosis, and a narrower question than the one this project started with.
organic_distance_to_target.per_country_refinement: FOLLOW-UP, reported as a NEGATIVE RESULT. The residual overshoot on oilseeds (1.40) and permanent crops (1.45) was attributed to applying CAPRI's 15-point EU shock uniformly, where CAPRI breaks it down by member state. Per-country organic shares were taken from Eurostat org_cropar as published (Austria 25.3%, Estonia 22.3, Sweden 20.4, Czechia and Italy 15.2, Latvia 14.8, Finland 13.5, Slovenia 10.0, Netherlands 3.7, Poland 3.5, Romania 2.9, Bulgaria 2.3, Ireland 1.6, Malta 0.5) and wired in, with the EU figure as fallback for the countries Eurostat does not name individually. The mechanism works: Italy now converts 9.8 percentage points instead of 15, and Austria converts nothing at all, being past the 25% target already. IT CHANGED ALMOST NOTHING: cereals -13.82 -> -13.90%, oilseeds -20.95 -> -21.06%, permanent crops -17.32 -> -17.42%. So the uniform EU shock was NOT the cause of the overshoot. The refinement is kept because it is more faithful to CAPRI and rests on published data, not because it improved the fit. The residual overshoot therefore remains unexplained: oilseed and permanent-crop AREAS contract more than CAPRI's (ours -9.9% and -4.9%, CAPRI's implied roughly -4.5% and -1%), while the yield channel matches (our cereal yield effect -11.5% against CAPRI's published -11%). Coverage of the per-country table is partial by design: 14 of 27 countries, stated rather than filled in by guesswork.

jrc121368_results_decomposition.status: obtained — the comparison basis this project lacked
jrc121368_results_decomposition.note: The published report was read in full from the user-supplied PDF (the online fetch truncated before the results). It gives the AREA/YIELD decomposition that every comparison here needed and none had: CEREALS - area -4%, yields -11%, supply -15%. The area effect breaks down further: landscape elements alone cause -9%, partly offset because farmers EXPAND cereal area to compensate for the lower yields from organic and reduced-pesticide production, and the GNB target adds +0.6% through reduced herds and feed demand. VEGETABLES AND PERMANENT CROPS - area REMAINS STABLE at +0.1%, while supply falls 12%, 'explained by the drop in yields, mostly due to the organic yield gap'. LIVESTOCK - meat supply -14%, raw milk -10%, dominated by the GNB target. AGAINST THIS MODEL: cereals production -13.9% against -15% and cereal area -2.4% against -4%, both close. But our vegetables and permanent crops lose 4.9% of AREA where CAPRI loses none, which is the whole of the remaining discrepancy - its production falls 12% purely on yields, ours falls 17.4% on yields PLUS an area contraction that should not happen. The question is no longer 'why do permanent crops under-respond' (they over-respond) but 'why does permanent-crop area move at all'. CAPRI notes that land-use cross effects from the arable sector positively affect fruit and vegetable areas, which is the mechanism to look at. ALSO CONFIRMED: Annex Table A3.3 reproduces exactly the organic yield gaps already loaded here from yield_effects_ppp.xlsx, including the PESETA region membership (Central Europe North = BE, DE, LU, NL, PL; Central Europe South = AT, CZ, FR, HU, RO, SK; Northern Europe = DK, EE, FI, LT, LV, SE; Southern Europe = BG, CY, ES, GR, HR, IT, MT, PT, SI; Ireland separate), which matches the mapping wired into supply_module. One independent check of that data passed.

wine_price_silent_drop.status: FIXED — the cause of the permanent-crop area discrepancy
wine_price_silent_drop.note: The regional producer-price file carries CAPRI's activity codes for five crops this model names differently - TWIN for wine, TEXT for cotton and other fibre, OFAR for fodder on arable - so those columns were never read and the crops silently fell back to the EU-wide price. The same silent-drop family as MAIZ/CORN, the grassland codes, and the herd aliases. WINE WAS THE DAMAGING CASE. CAPRI prices it at a median of 1,362 EUR/t (2,453 in the French appellation regions, 403 in Spain's largest wine region); the fallback was 95.5. That left wine on a NEGATIVE gross margin in the biggest wine regions - Spain -712, Aquitaine -1,413 EUR/ha - where real EU wine margins are strongly positive at 2,000-6,000. An activity sitting at a negative margin responds erratically to any cost shock. HOW IT WAS FOUND, by decomposition rather than inference: the permanent-crop group was contracting 4.9% in area where CAPRI reports it STABLE at +0.1%. Splitting the group showed the model was right about almost all of it - olives, the largest permanent crop at 4.5 Mha, moved -0.10%, matching CAPRI exactly; citrus -2.6%, other fruit -3.1%, apples -3.7%. The contraction was wine (-11.3%) and vegetables (-9.3%), and vegetables are annual crops whose mobility is expected. The permanent-land constraint never binds (0 of 248 regions), which ruled out the land-structure explanation. AFTER THE FIX: wine -11.32% -> -2.58%, true permanent crops -4.11% -> -1.73% against CAPRI's +0.1% for the combined group, and the whole group (with vegetables) -4.94% -> -2.93%. Production -17.4% -> -16.7% against CAPRI's -12%. Base fidelity, all 8 anchors, validator 12/0/0 and 51/51 tests unchanged. WHAT REMAINS, and why this is as far as the evidence goes: CAPRI has a wine price for only 147 of 248 regions, so the rest still use the EU fallback - Sicily is one of them. And the residual overshoot on production is now dominated by VEGETABLES, which are annual crops; CAPRI reports them combined with permanent crops, so the +0.1% reference cannot be split to check them separately.

manifest_coverage_gap.note: Five inputs added during 2025-26 development were loaded and used but declared in NEITHER manifest: livestock_output_coef, livestock_revenue_coef, nutrients_regional, organic_yield_gap and capri_own_price_elasticities. INPUT_MANIFEST.json documents what each input is; MANIFEST.json carries the expected row and column counts that the validator checks. Missing from both, the files were invisible to the shape check - so a truncated or missing livestock coefficient file would have passed validation silently, which is precisely the failure mode the manifest exists to catch and which this project has hit repeatedly. Found while updating the README, because the README claimed 'every input the model consumes is declared' and that claim turned out to be false. FIXED: all five declared in both manifests with concept, unit, dimension, CAPRI symbol and shape; capri_own_price_elasticities also registered in loaders._FILE_CATEGORY so the validator can resolve it (it is reference data the model does not load, but it is shape-checked like any other file). VERIFIED BY BREAKING IT ON PURPOSE: truncating livestock_revenue_coef.csv to 99 rows now raises '99 rows (manifest 248)'; removing a file fails the presence check. The validator went from 25 to 30 files covered, and still reports 12 pass / 0 warn / 0 fail on the intact data.

schema_coverage_verified.status: claim verified and its scope corrected
schema_coverage_verified.note: The README's '99.4% of live cells are real CAPRI data' was checked rather than carried forward. Two problems. First, INPUT_SCHEMA.json declared 22 inputs while INPUT_MANIFEST.json declared 29, and a README edit had changed the count to 29 in a sentence that refers to the SCHEMA - so the stated number was wrong for the file it named. Second, and more substantive, the coverage figure was computed over those 22 inputs only: the five inputs added during development were outside it, so the headline percentage described a subset of the data layer rather than all of it. FIXED: all seven missing inputs declared in INPUT_SCHEMA.json with concept, unit, dimension, consuming modules, source and known gaps, so the schema and the manifest now agree at 29. Four apparent differences between the two files were only naming (schema 'trade_flows' against manifest 'trade_flows_2021.csv', and three similar). RECOMPUTED over the whole data layer: 123,159 real cells of 123,758 declared, 99.5%. The claim holds, and now means what it says. The README cites the tool that produces it (tools/verify_schema.py) so the next reader can re-run it rather than trust it.

rice_market_and_minor_activities.status: both closed — the model now reproduces CAPRI's agricultural area exactly
rice_market_and_minor_activities.note: TWO OPEN POINTS CLOSED TOGETHER, both bounded data work. RICE NOW HAS A MARKET. Paddy rice was an activity competing for land but not a market commodity, so it had no trade balance and no price feedback. The data was already held: CAPRI's own world price (capmod_world_prices_2017.csv, RICE 411.42 EUR/t) and FAO production, consumption and trade for 24 regions in the extended SUA file. PARI is now a market commodity with Armington parameters taken from other cereals, the nearest analogue. World rice balances exactly at 386,384 kt with the real producers - China 141,643, India 112,221, Indonesia 36,798, Vietnam 28,481. One alias was needed: FAO names paddy rice RICE while this model's activity is PARI, and reading the file without it would have dropped rice silently - the same failure as MAIZ/CORN and TWIN/WINE. THE FOUR REMAINING CAPRI ACTIVITIES ARE MAPPED: other marketable crops (1,154 kha), other industrial crops (268), nursery plants (181) and flowers (118). They had been left out deliberately rather than folded into crops they are not; CAPRI holds complete areas, yields, costs and prices for all four, so they are now activities in their own right. The model has 34 crop activities. RESULT: the model's agricultural area equals CAPRI's EXACTLY - 166,690 kha against 166,690, 100.0%, where it was 99.0%. Every CAPRI crop activity with a recorded area is mapped. The manifest earned its keep here: adding rice changed the row counts of world_prices.csv and armington_params.csv, and the shape check flagged both before anything else could absorb them silently. Shapes updated; validator 12/0/0, all 8 anchors hold, base fidelity 0.58%.

oilseed_permanent_overshoot.note: On CAPRI's own reporting basis (production, EU-wide, all 248 regions, converged): cereals -13.9% against CAPRI's -15% (0.93), oilseeds -21.1% against -15% (1.40), permanent crops and vegetables -16.7% against -12% (1.39). Cereals are close; the other two OVERSHOOT. WHAT IS NOT THE CAUSE, each ruled out by measurement rather than argument: the yield channel (our cereal yield effect is -11.5% against CAPRI's published -11%); land pinning (the arable shadow price is zero in all 248 regions); price feedback (without it cereals fall 7.0% instead of 5.9%); supply elasticities (they match CAPRI's own regional PELA values at 0.76-1.00, median 0.92); a uniform organic shock (applying CAPRI's 15 points per country from Eurostat organic shares moved the result by less than 0.2 percentage points); and catch crops (CAPRI models them as a winter-cover share, not a land competitor, and they REDUCE pest damage). WHERE THE RESIDUAL SITS. Decomposing the permanent-crop group: olives, the largest at 4.5 Mha, move -0.10% against CAPRI's 'stable'; citrus -2.6%, other fruit -3.1%, apples -3.7%. The contraction is concentrated in VEGETABLES at -9.3% - annual crops whose mobility is expected and which CAPRI reports MERGED with permanent crops. Its +0.1% reference for the combined group therefore cannot be split to check vegetables separately. WHY THIS IS AS FAR AS THE EVIDENCE GOES: closing it needs CAPRI's results per product, which the published report does not give at that resolution, and a CAPRI scenario run is not available. The remaining 1.39-1.40 is the limit of what this comparison can resolve, not a located defect. FOR THE USER: treat oilseed and permanent-crop scenario magnitudes as overstated; cereals, the yield channel and the area response are close to CAPRI.

livestock_intensity_margin.status: implemented and pinned by a test
livestock_intensity_margin.note: CAPRI carries every dairy herd twice, as a low- and a high-intensity variant (DCOL and DCOH). In the base year the split is MECHANICAL - the two levels are exactly half the herd in every region checked - and their yields average to the dairy yield this model already used (DE11: 6,287 and 10,481 kg/head, average 8,384). So representing them separately adds nothing to the base year. What they carry is a RESPONSE CHANNEL: a herd can move between intensities under policy, which is how CAPRI lets dairy extensify under a nutrient target instead of only shrinking. Without it the only livestock margin is the number of animals. IMPLEMENTED as an intensity margin rather than as extra activities, matching how crop nitrogen intensity is already handled: CAPRI's per-region DCOL and DCOH yields are extracted to livestock_intensity_bounds.csv (235 regions, EU median 5.39 and 8.99 t milk/head), and a nitrogen ceiling moves the dairy yield toward the low-intensity bound by the same pressure the crops face.
